inst.title: Rules of Conduct - Uniformed Personnel
b: This instruction prescribes The City University of New York policies for conduct of University-wide Public Safety Department officers established by the University Director of Public Safety for the effective administration of campus public safety operations.

These policies have been formulated within the scope and intent of the University Public Safety Department. Failure to comply with these policies, instructions and guidelines may result in a recommendation to appropriate college officials that disciplinary charges be filed. In addition to the rules of conduct contained in this instruction, members of the service are subject to specific rules of conduct outlined in Operation Instruction # 11 – Summary Penalties for Violations of Rules of Conduct.
UNIVERSITY POLICIES FOR CONDUCT OF PUBLIC SAFETY PERSONNEL

Campus Peace Officers and Campus Security Assistants must promptly obey all lawful and proper orders and instructions written or otherwise, however transmitted or received, from their supervisors. This includes orders from the presidents and vice presidents of colleges to which the officers are assigned.

Campus Peace Officers and Campus Security Assistants are prohibited from engaging in conduct which is disruptive, inappropriate, unprofessional, or detrimental to his/her duties as a Peace Officer or Security Officer

Campus Peace Officers and Campus Security Assistants shall be dignified and courteous in their dealings with other members of the service and all other employees and students of The City University of New York.
Campus Peace Officers and Campus Security Assistants shall conduct themselves with dignity and courtesy at all times.

Campus Peace Officers and Campus Security Assistants shall be honest, truthful and accurate. They shall be responsible for submitting written and/or oral reports that are accurate. Officers will not submit false statements or statements which are intended to be misleading.
Campus Peace Officers and Campus Security Assistants shall treat as confidential all official public safety or law enforcement-related business.

College Public Safety Directors must immediately notify, in person or by phone, the President of their college and the University Public Safety Director of any campus officer who is arrested or is required to appear before any court or regulatory agency to answer a charge or to appear as a witness, arising out of any incident in which the officer is involved, on or off duty. Campus Peace Officers and Campus Security Assistants must immediately notify their College Public Safety Directors by telephone or in person, of such incident, giving basic facts of the incident, or if unable to comply personally, shall have a responsible person make immediate notification.

A Campus Peace Officer who, under color of office, becomes involved while off duty in any situation which could or does result in either an arrest or an altercation (verbal or physical) will immediately notify his College Public Safety Director, by telephone, of the incident. He will then prepare and forward a written report of the details of the incident to the College Public Safety Director for review.

When a campus officer becomes aware of information concerning illegal activity in another college's jurisdiction, he will promptly bring such information to the attention of his College Public Safety Director. The College Public Safety Director will forward such information to the proper authorities. If the information is a threat of imminent danger to life and property outside the officer's presence, the officer should promptly call the information to the attention of the responsible College Public Safety Director, then notify his College Public Safety Director. In the event that the College Public Safety Director is not available, the officer will notify the University Public Safety Director.
All officers shall cooperate in all investigations conducted by a duly appointed investigatory body or official of the College or University, except as may be protected by law.
Campus Peace Officers must carry their CUNY Peace Officer identification cards at all times.

Campus Peace Officers and Campus Security Assistant’s must have on their person at all times the shield issued by the Office of the University Director of Public Safety. When in uniform, it shall be worn on the outermost uniform garment over the left breast.

The loss of a Peace Officer or Campus Security Assistant shield and/or identification card shall be reported at once to the College Public Safety Director and the University Director of Public Safety. In addition, the loss shall be reported at once to the jurisdiction of the Police Department in the area where the card or shield was believed to be lost.

Campus Peace Officers and Campus Security Assistants on duty will be properly uniformed and neat and clean in their personal appearance. When in uniform, the uniform hat may be left off while a member is operating a patrol vehicle or in a college building (with the permission of the College Public Safety Director), but must be worn immediately upon leaving the vehicle or building. The wearing of beards and goatees are prohibited. Mustaches shall be neatly trimmed. (See University Public Safety Operation Instruction Number 5.0)

Campus Peace Officers and Campus Security Assistants on duty shall not be absent from duty without official leave; such leave shall be approved in compliance with F.L.S.A. standards, University Personnel Rules, Regulations and Policies and such additional college policies as may be in force.

Campus Peace Officers and Campus Security Assistants shall be punctual in reporting for duty and in maintaining assigned work schedules and shall not disrupt staffing due to excessive absence. For purposes of this section, excessive absence shall be defined as four (4) unscheduled absences in a six month period.
Officers intending to engage in any outside employment shall first obtain joint approval from his College Public Safety Director and College Human Resources Director.

Campus Peace Officers and Campus Security Assistants, in uniform, shall not carry an umbrella, package, or like object, except when necessary for the performance of duty. Carrying or use of cell phone or other electronic communications devices without express authorization of the College Director of Public Safety is prohibited.

Campus Peace Officers and Campus Security Assistants, on duty, shall not engage in reading or writing except job related material, forms, etc. explicitly provided by their supervisors or such incidental items as may be requested by a member of the college community (e.g., a note, a message, etc.).
Campus Peace Officers and Campus Security Assistants shall not sleep during assigned work tours except with specific authorization.
Campus Peace Officers and Campus Security Assistants are prohibited from smoking in public view while in uniform.
Campus Peace Officers and Campus Security Assistants shall not engage in gambling of any form while on duty or on University or college property.

Campus Peace Officers and Campus Security Assistants, under color of office, shall not solicit rides, services, or anything of value from anyone for personal gain except as directed by a supervisor in connection with the performance of necessary public safety or law enforcement duties.

Campus Peace Officers and Campus Security Assistants shall not accept awards, gratuities, or any article of value as payment for favors or services rendered in connection with their official duties except such awards, etc. that are conveyed by the college or University in accordance with University Public Safety or Personnel Rules, Regulations and Policies.
Campus Peace Officers and Campus Security Assistants, under color of office, shall not attempt to sell or exchange anything.

Campus Peace Officers and Campus Security Assistants shall not lend money or anything of value for gain to other members of the CUNY Public Safety Department or other college employee, student or staff person.

Campus Peace Officers and Campus Security Assistants shall not knowingly, except in the discharge of their official duties, associate, fraternize or transact any business or have any dealings whatsoever with known criminals, racketeers, gangsters, gamblers, or persons engaged in unlawful pursuits or activities.
Campus Peace Officers and Campus Security Assistants shall not drink intoxicants while in uniform or on duty.
When a Campus Peace Officer or Campus Security Assistant is apparently intoxicated or disabled by alcohol, a superior officer shall:
If the Campus Peace Officer or Campus Security Assistant is reporting for duty, not permit him/her to perform duty.
If the Campus Peace Officer or Campus Security Assistant is on duty, relieve the officer from duty.

Campus Peace Officers and Campus Security Assistants shall not use any unlawful substance or intoxicants, at any time, or in any form (i.e. marijuana, heroin, cocaine, alcoholic drinks), while on duty or while in uniform, nor shall they, at any other time, use intoxicants to an extent that they render the officer unfit for duty at the start of their assigned work tour.

Campus Peace Officers and Campus Security Assistants shall not bring, or permit to be brought, any unlawful substance, dangerous drugs or intoxicants onto a college or University facility. Neither shall an officer bring, or cause to be brought, any unlawful substance, dangerous drugs or intoxicant for his personal use while on duty.

Unless in the immediate performance of patrol duty, Campus Peace Officers and Campus Security Assistants, in uniform, shall not enter any Premises which are used for the manufacture, storage, shipping or sale of intoxicants, except for the purpose of eating a meal in a duly licensed restaurant.

Campus Peace Officers and Campus Security Assistants shall not possess any intoxicant on any college facility or in any college or University vehicle or equipment, unless specifically authorized to do so by the college president or designee.

Campus Peace Officers who have been authorized by the president of a college to bear firearms shall never brandish weapons nor shall they remove firearms from holders or holsters other than in the proper performance of duty in accordance with the NYS Penal Law Article 35 and the justification for the use of a deadly physical force (see Operations Instruction # 3).
Campus Peace Officers and Campus Security Assistants shall be responsible for the good care, proper maintenance, and serviceable condition of CUNY/college property issued or assigned to their use.

Campus Peace Officers and Campus Security Assistants shall promptly report to the College Public Safety Director the loss of, damage to, or unserviceable condition of any CUNY/college property issued or assigned to the officer.

Public Safety Department equipment shall be issued only for official purposes and used for the purposes for which it is designated. The equipment will be used only by the campus officer to whom it has been assigned, unless otherwise directed by a college public safety supervisor or higher authority. Except when necessary in an emergency, standard equipment furnished by the University/College shall not be changed nor shall anything be added thereto or taken there from.

inst.title: Use of Code Signals – Public Address Systems
b: The purpose of this instruction is to provide a standard set of code signals to be used in summoning emergency or other assistance by means of radio or public address systems.

All code signals contained herein are classified as confidential and their meaning should be disclosed to no one except those individuals whose duties are to respond to a given signal. All requests for public safety department must be cleared by the Campus Public Safety Communications Desk or Public Safety Director’s Office.

Students or campus staff members requiring assistance, should be instructed to call the Public Safety Communications Desk/office or, at those campuses where the public safety office is not staffed 24 hours a day, the transmission point designated by the Campus Public Safety Director.

Whenever possible, persons requesting assistance should identify themselves, state the location where the response is requested, and the circumstances necessitating the request. It shall be the Campus Public Safety Director’s responsibility to inform the college community as to how to request public safety assistance.

Members of the Public Safety Department are responsible for thoroughly familiarizing themselves with the meaning of each code, and the manner in which calls for service are to be handled at their campus of assignment.
Members of the service may request from the Public Safety Desk, any response provided by the code system.

Campus officers assigned to Communications Desk duty, their reliefs or other personnel designated to dispatch assistance will, after judging the facts received from the person requesting assistance, broadcast the code signal which is appropriate.
The use of code signals involving civilian participation should be cleared by a ranking public safety officer.

All requests for NYPD assistance must be in accordance with protocols regarding Police Response to Campuses established by the Chancellor and promulgated in a memorandum to all college presidents dated March 24, 1992. These requests must be recorded in the campus public safety telephone log, or other recording mechanism, so long as the information can be retrieved.
Campus Public Safety Directors may institute signal codes in addition to those specified if deemed necessary for the efficient operation of the college, provided that:
the codes as listed are not changed; and
codes established by Campus Public Safety Directors do not conflict with code numbers used at any other campus.
On occasion, when a “special duty” detail is assigned to a college, a special code number may be assigned to be used for the purpose of contacting a member of that detail.
PAGING AT CAMPUS FACILITIES WITH PUBLIC ADDRESS SYSTEMS

The Campus Public Safety Director of a college with a public address system will, after evaluating the specific needs of his campus, establish procedures for public safety utilization of the college's public address system, pursuant to authorization by the college president or designee.

During an event requiring mobilization other than mobilization of the SAFE Team, officers
visiting the event location will be afforded the Call Sign “Task Force” followed by a number.
For example, if City College mobilized three officers to LaGuardia Community College they

accommodate all visiting officers. Under this scenario, LaGuardia Community College’s Central Dispatch would write down the visiting officer’s name, accompanied by his/her task force number on the central dispatch plotting sheet. This will enable the dispatcher to identify officers and their assignments.

inst.title: Use of Firearms and Deadly Physical Force
b: The City University of New York recognizes the value of all human life and is committed to respecting the dignity of every individual. The primary duty of all members of the service is to preserve human life. The authority to carry and use firearms on a CUNY college campus can only be granted by the respective college presidents and is an awesome public safety and law enforcement officer responsibility. The most serious act in which a peace officer can engage is the use of deadly force. Respect for human life requires that, in all cases firearms be used as a last resort and then only to protect life.

The term Deadly Physical Force when used in this instruction, is defined as physical force which, under the circumstances in which it is used, is readily capable of causing death or serious physical injury. The discharge of a firearm always constitutes deadly physical force.
Offense, when used in this instruction, is defined as conduct for which a sentence to a term of imprisonment or a fine is provided pursuant to law.
USE OF FIREARM OR OTHER DEADLY PHYSICAL FORCE

Peace officers shall not use deadly physical force against another person, unless they have probable cause to believe that they must protect themselves or another person present from imminent death or serious physical injury.

Only the minimal amount of force necessary to protect human life should be used by uniformed members of the service. Where feasible, and consistent with personal safety, a warning, such as “Peace Officer, Don’t Move” should be given. Deadly force is never justified in the defense of property. The safety of the public and the uniformed members of the service must be the overriding concern whenever the use of firearms is considered.

New York State Criminal Procedure Article 2 Section 2.10 Sub Section 79 - Persons Designated as Peace Officers. Peace Officers appointed by the City University of New York pursuant to subdivision sixteen of section sixty-two hundred six of the education law, who shall have the powers set forth in section 2.20 of this article whether or not they are acting pursuant to their special duties; provided, however, that nothing in this subdivision shall be deemed to authorize such officer to carry, possess, repair or

dispose of a firearm unless the appropriate license therefor has been issued pursuant to section 400.00 of the penal law, to wit a Security Guard Carry License issued by the License Division of the New York City Police Department. This license restricts the carry of the firearm only while engaged in official duties. The weapon may be carried to and from the officer’s residence only with the approval of the College Public Safety Director or the University Director of Public Safety
SPECIFIC RESTRICTIONS ON THE USE OF FIREARMS

Reckless or negligent conduct An officer may not use his firearm if its use would in any way unjustifiably endanger innocent persons whom he is not seeking to arrest or retain in custody. If in using his firearm, an officer consciously disregards or fails to perceive a substantial and unjustifiable risk of injury to innocent persons, he may be held liable for the consequences of reckless conduct or criminal negligence. A firearm must never be removed from its holster unless its immediate use is permitted. The display or brandishing of a firearm for the purpose of warning, intimidation, or engaging in horseplay constitutes usage and is strictly prohibited. Care and good judgment must be exercised in all instances involving the discharge of firearms.
Warning shots The firing of warning shots is prohibited.

Discharging a firearm from or at a moving vehicle Discharging a firearm from or at a moving vehicle is prohibited unless the occupants of the other vehicle are using deadly physical force against the officer or another, by means other than the vehicle.
Property Peace officers shall not discharge their firearms or use any other form of deadly physical force in defense of property.
Summoning assistance Peace officers shall not discharge their firearms to summon assistance.

Animals Peace officers shall not discharge their firearms at or use any other form of deadly physical force against a dog or other animal except to protect themselves or another person from imminent death.
Authorized weapons and ammunition While on duty, officers will carry only weapons and ammunition authorized and issued by the CUNY Department of Public Safety.

Fleeing persons Peace officers shall not discharge their firearms or use any other form of deadly physical force to subdue a fleeing felon who presents no threat of imminent death to themselves or another person present.
When carrying a firearm, an officer shall carry the firearm on one’s person in an authorized holster in good working order, which will not allow access to the weapon by an unauthorized person.

When the firearm is carried in the course of official duty, the firearm is to be fully loaded with authorized ammunition. The weapon shall be carried with a round in the chamber with a fully loaded magazine.
Officers shall not be in possession of a firearm if they are, or if there is any possibility they become unfit for duty because of intoxicants.
Any officer who reasonably believes that another officer may be unfit for duty shall immediately inform a supervisor and record his or her observations in writing.

The supervisor shall immediately take appropriate steps to address the allegation including: conducting an investigation of the allegation, if the supervisor is responsible for conducting such internal investigations, to determine whether the officer is or was in violation of this section in light of all credible relevant information; and/or immediately notifying the unit within the department responsible for internal investigations. This would include the notification of the New York City Police Department (NYPD) License Division Incident Section of the alleged violation.

In conducting an investigation of the allegation, credible relevant information may include statements of the officer at issue, other officers or employees, or other witnesses; any Breathalyzer or other test results available; the supervisor’s own observations; and the time elapsed since the alleged misconduct.

If a supervisor or other investigating entity determines that the employee is unfit for duty, or that the officer has violated these guidelines, then the officer’s firearm privileges shall be suspended and firearm and ammunition seized by the department Gun Custodian.

Any officer who is or has been found to be in violation of this section, whether or not firearm privileges are suspended, shall be referred to agency counseling services or to other health care providers. The officer may also contact such counseling services or health care providers directly.

If an officer receives psychiatric treatment or treatment for alcoholism or Drug abuse, or is the subject to any disability or condition that may affect the ability to safely possess or use a firearm, the employee is required to notify the department immediately. In addition immediate notification must be made to the New York City Police Department License Division Incident Section of the treatment, disability or condition. The officer must surrender the firearm to the department gun Custodian until they are found to be fit for duty.

If a firearm is not being carried, it must be properly secured in a manner which minimizes the risk that an unauthorized person may readily obtain it. New York City Administrative Code Section 10-312 makes it a criminal violation for any person who is the lawful owner or lawful custodian of a firearm to store or otherwise place or leave such weapon in such a manner or under such circumstances, that it is out of his or her immediate possession or control, without having rendered the weapon inoperable by employing a safety locking device, such as a trigger lock, a combination handle, or a gunlock.

Firearms must be safeguarded at all times and may not be left in an unattended motor vehicle, desk drawer, locker or filing cabinet, other than a locker provided for that purpose in a secured department facility.

Employees who are hospitalized on an emergency basis shall as soon as practicable notify the department of their hospital stay so that appropriate arrangements for retrieval and temporary safeguarding of the firearm may be made by the department.

Any officer who loses a service firearm either through theft or other circumstances whether inside or outside New York City, shall immediately report said incident to the police precinct having jurisdiction over the geographic location where the loss occurred. After notifying the police precinct, the officer shall immediately report the loss to Public Safety Headquarters as well as their College Public Safety Director. The department Gun Custodian will then make the necessary notification to the NYPD License division Incident Section of the loss or theft. Thereafter an investigation is conducted by the Public Safety Department as well as the Police Department and License Division.
SUSPENSION AND REVOCATION OF FIREARMS PRIVILEGES
The following circumstances may result in the suspension and/revocation of firearm privileges:
Improper discharge or public display of unholstered firearm;
Receipt of psychiatric treatment or treatment for alcoholism or drug abuse or the presence of any disability, or other condition that may affect the ability to possess or use a firearm;
Failure to properly safeguard, including loss, theft, improper handling, or failure to utilize required safety locking device.
Arrest, indictment, or conviction, inclusive of a desk appearance ticket and of a summons other than a traffic infraction;

Officer becomes the subject or recipient of an order of protection, including a temporary order of protection, or an order of suspension or ineligibility under Criminal Procedure Law Section 530.14 or Family Court Act Section 842-a;
Loss or theft of firearms license;
Alteration, mutilation or destruction of a firearms license; or

Whenever the Public Safety Department determines that an employee is unfit to possess a firearm, the employee’s firearms privileges shall be revoked. A report indicating the grounds for the determination shall be given to the employee (who shall be requested to sign and date acknowledging receipt of such report). The report shall be placed in the employee’s personnel file; and the NYPD License Division.

The firearms privileges of an officer may be temporarily suspended pending investigation and final decision in a case of alleged unfitness for duty (as described in Section VI.1 above) or if it appears that one of the grounds for revocation in Section VIII.A above exists and that suspension is appropriate under the circumstances, or if an officer’s license to possess a firearm permit has been suspended by the NYPD License Division.
Officers shall not be eligible for the restoration of their firearms privileges unless:

All charges against the officer that were related to the revocation of the privileges have been adjudicated and the officer is not on probation for an offense/incident which led to the revocation of the privilege or subject to any of the conditions or circumstances listed in Section VIII.A.
Any officer requesting to have his/her firearm privileges restored shall submit documentation and evidence relevant to the grounds of the revocation, which may include:
Copy of the Police Department’s complaint/arrest report;
Copy of desk appearance ticket or summons;
Certificate of Disposition from the concerned court; or
Upon receipt of such a request:

The request shall be forwarded to the officer’s immediate supervisor or other designated responsible party within the agency, who shall investigate and review the request and make a written recommendation as to whether the request shall be granted or denied and specify reasons In the course of the investigation and review the responsible party may confer as appropriate with other agency employees including medical, legal and operational personnel. The request and recommendation shall then be forwarded to the University Director of Public Safety.

The University Director of Public Safety shall review all factors and circumstances and determine whether the firearm privilege should be restored. The request with all attachments and a written order noting the final determination and its grounds, including copies of all documents considered, shall be retained in the officer’s personnel file.
The department may order an employee to undergo an independent medical and/or psychological examination before restoring a firearm.

Before any firearm or ammunition is returned to an officer the department shall confirm the officer’s status with the NYPD License Division and determine whether the officer is under investigation or has had his or her license suspended or revoked.

Once approval is granted and subject to any necessary re- qualification by the officer, the officer’s firearm and ammunition will be inspected and returned. The officer will be required to sign a receipt for the items returned.

Officers who are authorized to carry a firearm must pass a firearm qualification course annually. Should an officer fail to qualify, his/her firearm will remain with the agency’s gun custodian until such time as the officer receives additional training and is able to qualify.
COMMUNICATION WITH THE NEW YORK CITY POLICE DEPARTMENT

The department’s gun custodian is designated as the department’s point of contact with the NYPD for all information relevant to whether and under what circumstances an officer should have the privilege of carrying firearms. In his/her absence the point of contact shall be the agency head or designee.

The gun custodian shall forward to the University Director of Public Safety or designee any information that may be helpful in a determination regarding suspension, revocation, or restoration of firearm privileges.

New York City requires that all agencies whose peace officers are required to obtain firearms licenses in order to possess firearms in the course of their duties shall require every such peace officer to obtain a firearms license for such activity from the Police department, notwithstanding whether the officer is otherwise authorized or licensed to carry a firearm.

An officer licensed and authorized to carry a firearm must immediately inform the NYPD License Division Incident Section as well as the precinct of occurrence (or the relevant police department if the incident occurs outside New York City) upon the occurrence of the following incidents or circumstances:
Discharge or public display of unholstered firearm other than at an authorized firearms training session.
Failure to properly safeguard, including loss, theft, improper handling, or failure to utilize required safety locking device.
Loss or theft of firearms license, identification card or shield.
An officer licensed and authorized to carry a firearm must immediately inform the NYPD License Division Incident Section upon the occurrence of the following incidents or circumstances:
Arrest, indictment, or conviction, inclusive of a desk appearance ticket and of a summons other than a traffic infraction;

Officer becomes the subject or recipient of an order of protection, including a temporary order of protection, or an order of suspension or ineligibility under Criminal Procedure Law Section 530.14 or Family Court Act Section 842-a;
Receipt of psychiatric treatment or treatment for alcoholism or drug abuse or the presence of any disability, or other condition that may affect the ability to possess or use a firearm;
Alteration, mutilation or destruction of a firearms license;
Any suspension, revocation, or restoration of firearms privileges.
Any department seizure or return of firearms and ammunition;
Any voluntary surrender of a firearm or return of a voluntarily surrendered firearm;
Any investigation into whether an officer’s firearm privilege should be suspended or revoked and the outcome of any such investigation; or
Any other incident that could result in the revocation of firearm privileges as listed in Section VIII.A.

The gun custodian shall inform the NYPD License division semiannually of the information required by 38 RCNY 5-24(a)(3)(iii), including the names, badge/tax numbers, and identifying information of all CUNY officers who are licensed to possess the firearm by the NYPD.
Reports under this section to the NYPD and to any other agency or division requested by the Police Department shall be by telephone with follow up via fax.

A peace officer shall immediately report to his College Public Safety Director each incident involving the discharge of firearms by himself or by another person occurring in his presence and shall submit a detailed written report to the Public Safety Director with respect to each such incident. Each individual case will also be reviewed by the University Director of Public Safety.

Whenever a member of the service discharges his firearm in New York City or is the subject of an assault while in the action of performing his duty as prescribed by law, he shall prepare a NYCPD Firearm Discharge/Assault Report (PD 424- 151) in triplicate at the college of occurrence. For the purpose of this report ONLY, any instances in which a member of the Public Safety Department, while performing a lawful duty, is struck, shoved, kicked, menaced, or subjected to an act of reckless endangerment, whether injured or not, shall constitute an assault. (See Appendix A)

If the member of The City University of New York Public Safety Department is assaulted and unable to prepare the Firearm Discharge/Assault Report because of injury or death, the immediate supervisor on duty shall be responsible for the preparation of the report. Two (2) copies of the form shall be delivered to the local NYC police precinct after being reviewed by the College Public Safety Director. The original and one (1) copy is to be forwarded to the Office of the University Director of Public Safety at 555 W. 57th Street, Suite 1030, New York, New York 10019.

In all cases where a firearm is unholstered or discharged by a University Peace Officer, a written Public Safety Incident Report and a Weapon Discharged/Use Report shall be prepared in accordance with The City University of New York Public Safety procedures. It shall be prepared and submitted to the Office of the University Public Safety Director with all relevant facts within 24 hours of the incident.
CRIMINAL AND CIVIL LIABILITY FOR VIOLATION OF RULES

The use of firearms in violation of these rules, causing injury, may result in criminal charges of assault or homicide against the officer and the officer may subject himself to civil liability for any injuries caused.
DISCIPLINARY ACTION FOR VIOLATION OF RULES
Violation of the rules set forth in this instruction will result in disciplinary action, being taken against the officer.
A member of the service shall prepare three copies of this report whenever he:
Discharges a firearm other than at an authorized firearms range, or
Is the subject of an assault while performing a lawful duty.
Station House Supervisors shall review and sign the report prior to forwarding the original copy to the Chief Inspector, and two copies to the Personnel Safety Unit.

inst.title: Inspection and Defective Firearm Procedures
b: This instruction prescribes the steps to be taken during the inspection of a service firearm. Failure to comply with this policy, instruction and guideline may create a hazard and will result in a recommendation to appropriate college officials that disciplinary charges be filed.

Service firearms will only be inspected by a department firearms instructor or armorer; in the course of a College firearms inspection or during initial/proficiency qualifications. Any firearm deemed unsafe will be removed from service immediately until such firearm is repaired or replaced.
The member of the service designated for firearms inspection shall proceed to an unloading station (if available) or a location designated by a firearms instructor or armorer.

The member of the service shall unload the firearm and lock the slide to the rear to expose the chamber. The member shall then be approached by the firearms instructor or armorer to whom the officer shall then present the firearm, muzzle pointed down and grip pointed towards the firearm instructor or armorer, for inspection.
The firearm instructor or armorer shall first assure that the firearm has been unloaded, and shall then inspect the following items:
Barrel, cylinder, and frame for cleanliness.
The front and rear sights to ensure that they are not bent or loose.
The firing pin to determine that it is not bent.
The ejection rod to check that it is not bent.
The firing pin to ensure that it comes through the pressure plate.
The firearms instructor or armorer shall then check the holster for safe operating condition and serviceability.
The firearms instructor or armorer shall return the service firearm to the member in the same manner it was presented.
The member shall reload the firearm and place it in the holster (The member shall not turn around until this is done).
Adequate records of each firearms inspection shall be maintained by the Office of the University Director of Public Safety.
All repairs to departmental firearms will be made by a departmental armorer or University authorized gunsmith. Repairs shall always be within manufacturer specifications.

In the event a department owned firearm is deemed unsafe and not suitable for duty carry, the member of the service must cease carrying the firearm and notify the Director of Public Safety at his/her command and the Office of the University Director Public Safety.

The defective pistol will be delivered to the Office of the University Public Safety Director by the member of the service whom the pistol is licensed or by the University Gun Custodian. The Office of the University Director of Public Safety will make arrangements to have the defective pistol repaired, tested and returned to whom it is assigned.
Officers will not, in any way, alter or modify the trigger or any other part of a department issued pistol.

inst.title: Personal Appearance - Uniformed Campus Public Safety Personnel
b: All public safety personnel while appearing in uniform shall be clean shaven, have hair properly trimmed and be neat and clean in their general appearance.
Hair (Male) The hair will be trimmed in such a manner that:
It is tapered to the general shape of the head.
It does not extend to the collar line of the uniform nor cover the ears or eyebrows when combed.
The uniform cap sits securely around the crown of the head.

Hair (Female) Hair must be neatly groomed and clean. Hair may not visibly extend below the top of the shirt collar. The bulk length of hair must not interfere with the wearing of uniform or emergency headgear.
Sideburns Sideburns will be neatly trimmed and not extend below the bottom lobe of the ear. The base of the sideburns will be a horizontal line. The “mutton chop” style of sideburns is not permitted.
Mustaches The mustache will be neatly trimmed and not extend beyond the outline of the upper lip, extend beyond the corner of the mouth, or drop below the corner of the mouth.
Beards Beards, goatees or hairy growths below the bottom lip or on the chin are not permitted.
Earrings Earrings of any kind will not be worn by male or female uniformed members of the public safety department.
Neck jewelry Visible neck jewelry is not permitted.
Any uniformed member of the service may be considered for exemption on an individual basis pursuant to written request submitted to the Office of the University Public Safety Director.
Exemptions for medical reasons will also be reviewed and considered when requested in writing with accompanying medical documentation specifying a diagnosis and prognosis from a licensed physician.
Any facial hair approved under this exemption must not exceed ¼ inch in length.

inst.title: Search of Arrested Persons
b: The purpose of this instruction is to provide a uniform standard for the search of arrested persons by members of The City University of New York Public Safety Department. This instruction will set forth a uniform set of policies and procedures which will be followed by all members of the CUNY Public Safety Department when searching arrested persons. It provides guidelines for the public safety supervisor, as well as those engaged in the search of arrested persons. Failure to comply with these policies, instructions and guidelines may result in a recommendation to appropriate college officials that disciplinary charges be filed.

All individuals arrested by members of the CUNY Public Safety Department will be subjected to a thorough search by at least one member of the service in order to ensure the safety of the officer at the time of the arrest. Persons arrested will not be subjected to a strip search.

Frisk/Field A frisk should be conducted before or immediately after the arrested individual is rear- handcuffed to ensure the personal safety of the arresting/assigned officer and of the arrested person.
The arresting/assigned officer, in determining at what point it is appropriate to conduct this frisk must take into account:
the particular facts and circumstances surrounding the arrest;

This search should be a methodical, external examination of the arrested individual which will be made by the arresting/assigned officer by kneading his hand over the subject’s body feeling for weapons or other objects that might pose a potential danger, with special attention being paid, but not limited to, the waistband, armpit, collar, groin area and hair.
If an object is detected which, in the officer’s opinion, might constitute a weapon, the officer will reach into, under or over the clothing to remove this object.

Care and caution will be exercised by the officer while conducting the frisk and/or removing objects at this time, with special attention to needles, razors and other items in the clothing or on the body of the arrestee which could cause injury to the officer or other persons.

Members of the CUNY Public Safety Department are to be mindful that the purpose of this field/frisk search is primarily to ensure the safety of the arresting/assigned officer. Strip searches are not permitted.
Search at the College Public Safety Office/Area

Immediately upon arrival at the Public Safety/area, the arresting/assigned officer must report to the supervisor to inform him of the arrest and the circumstances which gave rise to the arrest. An arrested individual’s safety, while in the custody of campus officers, is the responsibility of the arresting/assigned officer and Public Safety Supervisor on duty. Regardless of the actions (violent or otherwise) of the arrested individual, sufficient and appropriate personnel will be assigned to ensure the safety of members of the service and to protect the arrested individual.

After arrival at the College Public Safety Office/area and reporting to the Public Safety supervisor, the arresting/assigned officer or a designated member of the same sex as the arrested individual will conduct a thorough search of the arrested individual’s person and clothing. The arrested individual will be requested to voluntarily empty his/her pocket (s) and surrender all items, contraband or otherwise on his/her person. The purpose of this search is to ensure the safety of all persons at the college. Therefore, all weapons, contraband and evidence not discovered during the field/frisk search should be removed from the arrested individual.
This College Public Safety Office/area search will consist of the following:
The arrested individual will be scanned as soon as practicable with a hand held electronic metal detector (if available).
All outer garments such as overcoats, jackets, sweaters, vests, hats, wigs, ties, belts, shoes, socks, handbags, and wallets will be removed and examined.
All pockets are to be emptied.
All clothing not removed will be examined by grabbing, crushing and squeezing the garments.
Should the hand held scanner detect an object, the following procedures will be used:
If the object detected is in the clothing or around the body of the arrested person, the object will be physically removed by the officer.

If the officer cannot locate the object which is causing a reading on the detector, he will immediately rear handcuff and transport the prisoner to the local NYPD Precinct. Upon arrival officers will immediately notify Precinct personnel of the potential weapon or object which has not been found.

A thorough search at the College Public Safety Office/area, as enumerated above, coupled with the electronic metal detector examination should eliminate the necessity of a full strip search for weapons, evidence or contraband and also ensure the safety and security necessary in balance with the constitutional rights of the individual in custody. In any case, strip searches by CUNY Public Safety personnel are prohibited.

Items lawfully carried on the arrested person and confiscated during the search at the Public Safety Office/area on the basis that the items might be used as a weapon or cause injury to the arrested person, peace officer, police or other arrested persons, or that could possibly deface or damage property, or facilitate escape, will be removed from the arrested person safeguarded and recorded. The arrested individual must be given a receipt for these items.
Items lawfully possessed by arrested individuals and removed by the arresting/assigned officer are not contraband.

Under no circumstances is a body cavity search (strip search) of an arrested individual to be conducted by any member of the CUNY Public Safety Department. If circumstances exist which cause the arresting officer or public safety supervisor to reasonably believe that the arrestee is secreting a weapon, contraband or other evidence in a body cavity, the prisoner will be immediately rear handcuffed and transported to the local NYPD Precinct where the campus public safety officer’s concerns and suspicions will be relayed to the Precinct Desk Officer.

Note: Since all CUNY Peace Officers are granted their peace officer powers in the Criminal Procedure Law of New York State under the auspices of the New York City Police Commissioner, they are mandated to follow and obey the rules and regulations of the New York City Police Department. Any arrestee brought into an NYPD precinct comes under the direct authority/jurisdiction of the desk officer of that precinct.

inst.title: Reasonable Suspicion Drug Testing Policy for CUNY Public Safety Personnel
b: All members of The City University of New York Public Safety Department perform a sensitive and critical role in providing for the public’s safety. The City University of New York has a long-standing commitment to the proper and efficient performance of that role. The use of illegal drugs on the part of members of the Public Safety Department destroys the proper and efficient performance of that role by undermining the job performance of the drug user and jeopardizing the safety of the user, other members of the service, other employees, the campus community and the public. It also weakens community confidence in the system and significantly interferes with the mission of The City University of New York Public Safety Initiative. Illegal drug use affects all segments of society and thus could affect officers or other members of the law enforcement discipline. Accordingly, it is essential that reasonable suspected illegal drug use by a member of the Public Safety Department be dealt with properly and effectively.

Nothing contained herein is meant to prevent or prohibit a sworn peace officer from taking enforcement action in the event he or she observes a crime or has probable cause to believe a crime is taking place or has taken place.

This Operation Instruction (O. I.) does not apply to the sale, use manufacture, distribution, or possession of alcohol, spirits, liquor, wine, beer, or impairment there from, which matters are covered by The City University of New York policies.
No member of the Public Safety Department shall use illegal drugs under any circumstances. (See IV below for definition).
No member of Public Safety Department shall use drugs (see IV below, for definition) on City University of New York property and/or while on duty except pursuant to Paragraph D below.
No member of the Public Safety Department shall report for duty impaired by drugs.
Violation of any of these prohibitions will lead to disciplinary action, with a recommendation for termination of employment.

Members of the Public Safety Department who observe or have knowledge of another member violating this policy or being in a condition which might constitute a violation of this policy must promptly report this matter to the

affected member’s College Public Safety Director, Assistant Public Safety Director or such other College/University official as designated in college policy. The failure of a member to do so shall lead to disciplinary action.

If a supervisor reasonably suspects (see IV below, for definition) that a member of the service is in violation of this policy, the supervisor must follow the procedures outlined in this O. I. If approved to do so, the supervisor must require the employee to report immediately for a drug test to the lab designated by the University Personnel Office (currently)
Partners in Safety 408 West 45th Street-- (between 9th/10th Avenues) New York, NY 10036 Monday - Friday 0830 – 1630 hours Telephone: (212) 727-8637

or to another medical professional facility selected by The City University of New York (see IV below, for definition). If the suspicion occurs during non-business hours, a holiday or during the weekend, the member must be ordered to report immediately on the next day that the medical facility is open. A member’s failure to follow a supervisor’s directive to do so will lead to disciplinary action with a recommendation for termination of employment.

Members of the Public Safety Department using any drug that could potentially affect their performance, must inform their supervisor prior to the start of the member’s first tour of duty after commencement of such use. The failure to do so may lead to disciplinary action. Information regarding a member’s use of prescription drugs will be kept strictly confidential.

An office, locker, desk, file cabinet or other repository provided to a member of the Public Safety Department by The City University of New York on College/University property (including college/University vehicles) is the property of The City University of New York. Such offices, lockers, desks, file cabinets, or other repositories are furnished by The City University of New York exclusively for work-related materials. Thus, there is neither a superior claim of privacy nor a reasonable expectation of privacy on that part of any member of the Public Safety Department in connection with an office, locker, desk, file cabinet or other repository or vehicle furnished by The City University of New York or the contents thereof.
When there is a reasonable suspicion that a member of the Public Safety Department possesses illegal drugs in violation of this policy, The City University

of New York has the right to search the office, desk, locker, file cabinet, or other repository assigned to the member on College/University property or any City University of New York vehicle provided to a member of the Public Safety Department.

Monitoring job behavior and work performance is a supervisory responsibility. One purpose of this O. I. is to assist supervisors in responding to situations where there is reasonable suspicion that a violation of the policy set forth in II above has occurred. A prompt response to such a situation is necessary in order to maintain a safe and efficient work environment, ensure the safety of employees and the public, and preserve college constituency confidence in the Public Safety Department. These guidelines outline the general role of the supervisor in implementing this policy.
All supervisors have the responsibility to ensure that all employees are fit to perform all of their duties and are free from the influence of drugs.

Expert knowledge about the use of drugs is not necessary. Rather, supervisors must remain alert to changes in work behavior and work product. Some changes in work behavior to which one should be alert are set forth in Exhibit A, annexed hereto.

Reasonable Suspicion - Impairment on the Job If a supervisor has a reasonable suspicion that a member of the service may be impaired from performing his or her duties as a result of drug use, the supervisor will take the following action:
Have another supervisor from the college or from another college -- if a supervisor from the college is not on duty -- observe the impairment.
Notify the College Public Safety Director of the member’s college who shall notify the College Personnel Director and the University Public Safety Director or designee.

Order the member to accompany him/her to a private setting. If the member refuses to accompany the supervisor to a private setting, the member is to be warned that his/her refusal constitutes a failure to follow an order and will lead to discipline with a recommendation of termination of employment. If at all possible, such warning should be made in the
presence of another supervisor, and, in the case of an employee represented by a union, of a union representative. In any event, a witness should be present, if at all possible.

If the member continues to refuse to accompany the supervisor, after approval by the University Public Safety Director, University Deputy Public Safety Director or Borough Public Safety Coordinator, the member is to be advised that he/she is suspended pending further investigation and is to be temporarily relieved of his/her service firearm, shield, handcuffs, baton, O. C. (pepper) Spray and identification card. Arrangements are to be made for the member to be taken home or to another safe place, if his/her condition warrants it. In such cases, supervisors should use all reasonable means short of force to prevent the member from leaving on his/her own. If the member refuses to be taken home or to another safe place and insists on driving a vehicle, the supervisor shall take appropriate law enforcement action (Arrest for D.W.U.I.).
Provide union representation if the member requests it. Notify a union representative as soon as feasible.

Tell the member the reason for the meeting. Stress the seriousness of the situation. Give the member the following warning and ask the member to explain his/her condition. Advise him/her that, "all employees must cooperate in authorized investigations of any act, omission or occurrence in or upon The City University of New York property (including, but not limited to, misconduct, accidents, crimes and the like) provided, however, that an employee is not required to give evidence against him/herself in connection with the investigation of an alleged act of misconduct on his part. Disciplinary proceedings may be commenced against him/her and that anything (s) he says may be used in evidence in such proceedings."

Should the member fail to explain satisfactorily his/her condition and the University Public Safety Director or designee agrees that a basis for the reasonable suspicion exits, the member must immediately undergo a drug screening as provided in Section 2C above.
The current lab for such tests is Partners in Safety, 408 West 45th Street -- (between 9th/10th Avenues) New York, NY 10036 -- Monday - Friday 0830 – 1630 hours - Telephone: (212) 727-8637
After approval by the University Public Safety Director or designee, temporarily relieve the member of his/her service firearm, shield, handcuffs, baton, O.C. (Pepper) Spray and identification card.

After a determination by the University Public Safety Director that reasonable suspicion exists, the University Public Safety Director, or designee, shall notify the College President, College Personnel Director and such other persons as need be informed at this stage.

If the member refuses to undergo the drug screening, or if during the course of the drug screening the member does not cooperate fully with the medical professional facility, including the administering of the drug test, the member is to be warned by the supervisor that his/her refusal or lack of cooperation constitutes a failure to follow an order and will lead to the filing of disciplinary charges with a recommendation of termination of employment. If at all possible, such warning will be made in the presence of another supervisor, and, in the case of a member represented by a union, of a union representative. In any event, a witness should be present, if at all possible.

If the member continues to refuse either to undergo a drug screening or to fully cooperate therewith, and after approval by the University Public Safety Director or designee, the member is to be advised that (s) he is suspended for the remainder of the tour with penalties provided in the summary discipline policy. Within one day, the supervisor shall request that the College Personnel Officer issue a letter of suspension pending further investigation. Arrangements will be made for the member to be taken home or to another safe place, if his/her condition warrants it. In such cases, supervisors shall use all reasonable means short of force to prevent the member from leaving on his/her own. If the member refuses to be taken home or to another safe place and insists on driving a vehicle, the supervisor shall take appropriate law enforcement action. (Arrest for D.W.U.I.)

If the member consents to a drug screening, the member will be taken as soon as possible by the supervisor or designee of a supervisory rank to Partners in Safety, 408 West 45th Street -- (between 9th/10th Avenues) New York, NY 10036 -- Monday - Friday 0830 – 1630 hours - Telephone: (212) 727-8637. If the member requests it, a union representative, if immediately available, may accompany the member for observation.

At the completion of the drug screening, the member shall be advised that (s)he will be placed on leave with pay (following the summary penalty time) until the lab has completed the evaluation, at which time the University Public Safety Director or the University Personnel Director will be contacted with the results of the evaluation. Make no promises as to outcome. Arrangements shall be made by the supervisor for the member to be taken home or to another safe place.

If the drug test is positive, Partners in Safety or the designated medical professional facility shall notify the University Public Safety Director and the University Personnel Director or designee who shall direct the College Personnel Director to suspend the member without pay and notify the College Public Safety Director. The College Public Safety Director will be directed to initiate the disciplinary process through the appropriate Personnel Department with a recommendation for the termination of employment. With the exception of individuals involved in the disciplinary proceedings, the test results will be kept confidential.

If the drug test is negative, Partners in Safety or the designated medical professional facility shall notify the University Public Safety Director, or University Personnel Director, who shall notify the college personnel officer. The University Public Safety Director or designee shall provide for the return of the member's service firearm, shield and identification card and the sealing of the case folder, unless there are other matters which warrant it to remain active. The University Public Safety Director shall provide written notification to the member of the negative results and the member will be reinstated.

Reasonable Suspicion - Information and Investigation Should a supervisor receive or obtain information which indicates that a member of the service may be in violation of this policy, other than circumstances described in Section B above, the following process is to be followed:
The supervisor shall prepare a comprehensive report setting forth the information and any facts or circumstances which may be related thereto
and submit it to the College Public Safety Director of the member's college of assignment.

The College Public Safety Director shall review the report and, if the College Public Safety Director agrees that reasonable suspicion of a violation of this policy exists, (s) he shall seek the approval of the Borough Public Safety Coordinator for ordering the member to undergo a drug screening. After the Borough Public Safety Coordinator reviews the case, and believes reasonable suspicion exists, he shall consult with the Deputy University Public Safety Director, the University Public Safety Director and the Vice Chancellor for Legal Affairs prior to ordering the member to undergo the drug screening. All pertinent information is to be provided as part of this consultation.

Approval for ordering the member to undergo a medical evaluation will only be given after a careful determination that the report has established that reasonable suspicion of a violation of this policy exists. If such a determination is made, the University Public Safety Director or in his absence the Deputy University Public Safety Director shall notify the Deputy Chancellor that such a case is in progress.

If it is determined that reasonable suspicion of a violation of this policy exists, the University Public Safety Director or designee will meet privately with the suspected member. If the member is represented by a union and requests it, a union representative shall be provided. The Borough Public Safety Coordinator, the Deputy University Public Safety Director or University Public Safety Director shall give the member the previously cited "rule"; (Section B Paragraph 5) advise the member of the information concerning the basis for the reasonable suspicion of illegal drug use; inform the member that (s)he is being temporarily relieved of his/her service firearm, shield and identification card; and order him/her to go immediately to the Partners in Safety or to another medical professional at a facility designated by the Office of University Personnel to undergo a drug screening. If the Borough Public Safety Coordinator reasonably believes it is necessary in connection with the investigation of the suspected violation of this policy, (s)he will also have a search made of the office, locker, desk, filing cabinet, or other repository or vehicle provided to the member by the college or The City University of New York.
If the member refuses to undergo the drug screening, or if during the course of the drug screening the member does not cooperate fully with the

directive to see the medical professional or does not cooperate fully with the drug screening evaluation, including the drug test, the member is to be warned that his/her refusal or lack of cooperation constitutes a failure to follow an order and will lead to disciplinary action, with a recommendation for termination of employment. If at all possible, such warning should be made in the presence of another supervisor, and, in the case of a member represented by a union, of a union representative. In any event, a witness should be present, if at all possible.

If the member continues to refuse either to undergo a drug screening or to fully cooperate therewith, and after approval by the University Public Safety Director or designee, the member is to be advised that (s)he is suspended for the remainder of the tour with penalties provided in the summary discipline policy. Within one day, the supervisor shall contact the College Personnel Officer to issue a letter of suspension pending further investigation. Arrangements will be made for the member to be taken home or to another safe place, if his/her condition warrants it. In such cases, supervisors shall use all reasonable means short of force to prevent the member from leaving on his/her own. If the member refuses to be taken home or to another safe place and insists on driving a vehicle, the supervisor shall take appropriate law enforcement action (Arrest for D.W.U.I.).

If the member consents to a drug screening, the member will be taken by the supervisor or designee of a supervisory rank to Partners in Safety. If the member requests it, a union representative, if immediately available, may accompany for observation.

At the completion of the drug screening, the member will be placed on leave with pay (following the summary penalty time) until Partners in Safety has completed the evaluation, at which time the member will be contacted by the University Public Safety Director or the Deputy University Public Safety Director with the results of the evaluation. Make no promises as to outcome. Arrangements will be made by the supervisor for the member to be taken home or to another safe place, if his or her condition warrants it.

If the drug test is positive, Partners in Safety shall notify the University Public Safety Director or the University Personnel Director. The University Public Safety Director or the Deputy University Public Safety Director shall direct the College Personnel Director, through the Office of the University Personnel Director to suspend the member and initiate the
disciplinary process, with a recommendation for termination of employment.

If the drug test is negative, Partners in Safety shall notify the University Public Safety Director and the University Personnel Director. The University Public Safety Director shall provide for return of the member's service firearm, (if applicable) shield and O. C. (Pepper) Spray, and identification card and the sealing of the case folder unless there is other matters which warrant it to remain active.

Reasonable Suspicion: An opinion based on specific, objective facts and reasonable inferences drawn from those facts in light of experience. Reasonable suspicion must be articulable and cannot be based on a mere hunch. Reasonable suspicion must be of a specific person or persons.

Reasonable suspicion based upon observations of contemporaneous physical indications of possible drug use may be supported by observations of behavioral and/or performance changes over a period of time. Some of such behavioral and performance changes are listed in Exhibit A, annexed hereto.
Among the factors to be taken into consideration in determining reasonable suspicion are:
the reliability of the person or source providing the information;
the extent of any corroboration; and,
any other factors contributing to the suspicion or the lack thereof.
Not all of these factors must exist to find reasonable suspicion, but all must be examined.

Nothing stated herein shall affect the University's right to conduct a random drug testing program or pre-employment drug testing in conjunction with return to work, promotions and periodic physical examinations performed in furtherance of or pursuant to applicable laws, regulations, or University policy.

Work behavior and performance should be primary concerns of the supervisor. With respect to the effects of drug abuse on work behavior and performance, expert knowledge regarding drugs is not necessary, but the supervisor must remain alert to changes from the normal work pattern and/or the behavior of the member.

It is the responsibility of the supervisor to act in accordance with University guidelines for administering the Reasonable Suspicion Drug Testing Policy. It is important to take immediate steps, since delayed action can threaten the safety of employees and the public.

inst.title: Medal Awards and Recognition & Wearing of Medals, and Mourning Bands
b: All formal recognition shall be based on the positive impact that an act or accomplishment has had on the individual college campus and/or the University community as a whole. Outstanding service to the community at large, a public relations program that enhances the mission and image of The City University and its public safety departments are examples of recognizable endeavors.
A member of the Public Safety Department may be recommended for formal recognition by a supervisor, a fellow officer or a member of the college community.
A College Director of Public Safety may grant formal recognition in the grade of "Excellent Duty" and must endorse requests for all other awards before they can be granted.

The Public Safety Borough Coordinators in the borough where the college request originates may grant recognition in the grade of "Meritorious Duty" and must endorse requests for all other higher awards before they can be granted.
Commendation medals and the Medal of Honor may be granted by the University Director of Public Safety with the endorsement of the University Director of Personnel.
All requests for formal recognition will be prepared on a "Request for Formal Recognition" form (See Appendix A).
All requests for formal recognition will be processed in the college of occurrence and directed to the College Director of Public Safety.
The College Director of Public Safety will assign a college control number to all requests and maintain a log of such requests.
The College Director of Public Safety will assign requests to a ranking supervisory officer, operations coordinator or tour supervisor for investigation. The investigating officer shall:
provide a detailed narrative account of the incident,
interview members involved, including patrol supervisor when appropriate.

The College Director of Public Safety after consultation with the College Director of Personnel will make certain that completed recommendations are delivered to the University Director of Public Safety for review.
If the College Director of Public Safety disapproves a request, the Director will indicate the disapproval at the bottom of the request form and advise the officer of his decision.

If the requesting party or officer wishes to appeal the recommendation of the College Director of Public Safety, the officer may do so by preparing two copies of a typed letter explaining the grounds for the appeal. The original will be forwarded to the Public Safety Borough Director, the copy will be sent to the University Director of Public Safety.
Members of the Public Safety Department may be awarded recognition in the following categories:
University Public Safety Department Medal of Honor

Awarded to a member of the service who while performing a specific act, exemplifies extraordinary bravery in the face of circumstances which would surely have led to grave personal injury or the officers own death had the slightest miscalculation occurred. The act should be clearly beyond the normal requirements of the position.
University Public Safety Department Rescue Medal
Awarded to a member the service for a specific act or acts which directly lead to the saving of a human life and which can be documented by public health officials involved.
University Public Safety Department Commendation Medal

This medal is awarded for a specific act involving either imminent personal risk or exceptionally good judgment. In cases involving imminent personal risk, the risk need not be of the extreme nature required for award of the Medal of Honor, but it must be clearly beyond the normal requirements of the job. In cases involving good judgment the action taken should be clearly outstanding to the degree that highly undesirable consequences would have followed had the individual not exercised exceptionally fine judgment and initiative.
University Public Safety Department Meritorious Duty Medal

Recognizes specific performance which clearly surpasses the normal requirements of the job but is not quite of the caliber which would warrant award of the University Public Safety Department Commendation Medal.
The University Public Safety Department Meritorious Duty Medal may be awarded for:
An act of intelligent and valuable public safety department demonstrating tenacity or perseverance, or
Three (3) commendable and recognizable acts of service over a one year period, or
An act which demonstrates highly notable integrity, or
A highly commendable accomplishment contributing to the improvement of college public safety policy or problem solving.
University Public Safety Department Excellent Duty Medal

This medal is awarded to an individual who, in the course of carrying out a project or extended assignment as part of the normal work of the officer’s position, achieves results which are of such a superior nature that the officer clearly deserves special recognition. Characteristics of performance which are considered in determining the award include: ingenuity, resourcefulness, unusual insight into problem solving, exceptional diligence and thoroughness in producing completed staff work, and above-standard degrees of proficiency, craftsmanship or professional competence. Among the kinds of results recognized by the award are the submission of a device or method adopted which results in improved administrative or operational efficiency, reduced cost or better service to, or relations with the community in general.
University Public Safety Department Unit Citation Medal

This award is presented to the officers of a special unit or task force whose performance in carrying out a project, extended assignment, or during an unusual operation was so outstanding as to warrant special recognition. The nature of the task should be such that a cooperative effort by each member of the group was clearly involved in accomplishing the objective. Among the kinds of achievements in recognition of which the award is given are significant monetary savings or additional revenues, avoidance of loss of life or damage to University property, greatly improved service to, or relations with students, faculty or staff of the college community in general.

NOTE: The Unit Citation must be requested by the College Director of Public Safety and endorsed by their respective Public Safety Borough Coordinator before it can be considered by the University Director of Public Safety.
