inst.title: Use of Oleoresin Capsicum Aerosol [O.C.] Spray
b: The City University of New York recognizes and respects the value and special integrity of each human life. In vesting University Peace Officers with the lawful authority to use force to protect the public welfare, a careful balancing of all human interests is required.

This instruction prescribes The City University of New York policies for the use of Oleoresin Capsicum Aerosol Spray (O.C.) set forth by the University Director of Public Safety for the effective administration of campus public safety operations.

These policies have been formulated within the scope and intent of the University Public Safety Initiative. Failure to comply with these policies, instructions and guidelines may result in a recommendation to appropriate college officials that disciplinary charges be filed.

University Peace Officers shall use only that force that is reasonably necessary to effectively bring an incident under control, while protecting the lives of the officer or another. A variety of coercive options are available to University Peace Officers during confrontational settings. These are often referred to as the "force continuum". The techniques range from verbal persuasion or coercion to hand control procedures such as an escort or pain/pressure compliance holds, or the use of more aggressive measures involving O.C. or the baton/ASP. Every effort should be made to use verbal commands to compel the offender to follow the directions of the University Peace Officer. If this effort is met with physical resistance or the threat of physical resistance, and the use of force is justified as per the Penal Law and Criminal Procedure Law of the State of New York, O.C. may be used to prevent or end the threat, or effect an arrest. The use of Oleoresin Capsicum Aerosol Spray (O.C.) constitutes a use of force in defense of a person. Such use of O.C. is authorized only in those instances and under such circumstances as authorized by Law Pursuant to Article 35 of the Penal Law of the State of New York. It is important to understand that O.C. is another non-lethal force option as it pertains to the "force continuum". Depending on the situation facing the officer, other force options may be needed or other equipment required, to handle the confrontation. O.C., like other defensive equipment, does not work on everyone all of the time; nothing does! You will find that O.C. is an excellent force option that is very effective. O.C. has been proven nationally to be one of the most effective, operational tools made available to public safety personnel.

O.C. active agent is capsaicin, oils and resin which is a derivative of Cayenne Pepper which is a natural product listed in many food products. It is an organically based, less than lethal aerosol spray defensive weapon designed to cause a loss of intended thought process, coordination and upper body control.

O.C. is an inflammatory agent that will cause mucous membranes to swell, producing an almost immediate closing of the eyes. O.C. also produces a sensation of intense burning of the skin. Because of these effects, the subject can then be restrained/controlled with minimum physical contact. This reduces the risk of injury to the officer and the person restrained.

O.C. produces no major lasting effects (beyond 30-45 minutes). If a person takes longer than 30-45 minutes to recover, they should be immediately evaluated by medical personnel. If the subject requests medical treatment, EMS should be summoned immediately, and if required, the subject should be taken to a medical facility for examination.

O.C. has been successfully proven to be effective on most subjects under the influence of alcohol/drugs, emotionally disturbed persons, and other subjects who have reduced sensitivity to pain, all without causing permanent damage. Remember, it does not work on everyone.
All University Peace Officers must attend a certified training session approved by The City University of New York before being permitted to carry or use O.C. on duty.
All University Peace Officers authorized to carry O.C. must take part in all phases of the training in order to be certified.
A University Peace Officer is not permitted the use of O.C. unless qualified in its proficient use as determined by training procedures.

Only qualified and authorized sworn Peace Officers shall carry O.C. The device will be stored in its issued holster at all times. Any time the device is used, a Public Safety Incident Report will be filed and The University Public Safety Director and College Public Safety Director will be notified. University-issued O.C. will be carried only when on duty. When an officer is off duty, it will be stored in his or her locker. The O.C. canister will be the responsibility of the individual officer to keep safe and within his/her control while on duty. Any O.C. device that is lost or stolen will be reported immediately to the on duty supervisor and a Command Log entry will be made. All O.C. shall remain The City University of New York property and administrative control over it will be maintained by the University Director of Public Safety and his staff.
Parameters for use of Oleoresin Capsicum Aerosol Spray:

O.C. will be used only after every effort has been made to use verbal commands to compel the offender to follow the directions of the University Peace Officer. If these commands are met with physical resistance or the threat of physical resistance, and the use of force is justified as per the New York State Penal Law, Article 35, O.C. may be used to prevent/end the threat or effect the arrest.

Where deadly physical force is not authorized, officers should assess the incident in order to determine which non-deadly technique or weapon will best de-escalate the incident and bring it under control in a safe manner and to accomplish a lawful task.
University Peace Officers are authorized to use department approved non-deadly force techniques and issued equipment for resolution of incidents, as follows:
In self-defense or the defense of others.
To control and effect an unlawful situation safely and effectively, and arrest an offender when physical force is justified under law and City University guidelines.
To assist in taking control of a violent, emotionally disturbed person (E.D.P.) who is a danger to himself or others.
When lower levels of force are deemed ineffective.

O.C. produces a cone or stream shaped spray up to 8-12 feet. The spray should be directed at the subject's face with a one second burst. Do not discharge at distances of less than 3 feet-may cause injuries to soft body tissue. Under no circumstances should O.C. Spray be used on a non-compliant, but non- aggressive individual. Wind and weather conditions are factors that should be considered prior to using O.C. spray. Officers should use only the amount of O.C. needed to control the situation. The subject should not be allowed to get the advantage in a physical confrontation. Once the situation is under control and the subject has submitted to custody, the use of O.C. must be discontinued. It is the officer's responsibility to make every effort to relieve the subject's discomfort, after being exposed to O.C., by flushing the eyes and contaminated areas with clear cool water as per decontamination procedures.
If O.C. is used inside a building, officers should make every reasonable attempt to warn and remove bystanders from the area prior to use.

Pepper spray shall not be used on suspects who passively resist arrest. (E.g., going limp, offers no physical resistance). Do not use pepper spray on the elderly, young children, pregnant women or persons with known respiratory conditions.
USE WITH VIOLENT EMOTIONALLY DISTURBED PERSON (E.D.P.'S)
An attempt should be made to calm the E.D.P, through reasoning and verbal persuasion whenever possible.

Whenever an officer (s) is confronted with a violent E.D.P, O.C. may be used if the circumstances are such that attempts at other forms of physical restraint will likely result in injury to the subject or the officer (s).
When an E.D.P. is armed with a dangerous instrument or other weapons, O.C. may be used immediately to disarm and take control of the subject.

VIII. SECURING OF ARRESTEE
After the subject has been sprayed he or she should be verbally ordered to a standing or
prone handcuffing position. Assure them that they will be treated and that the effects will
dissipate shortly, then handcuff, using extreme caution. Regardless of the handcuffing
position chosen, an officer should approach the subject from the side or rear. Never from
the front.
IX.

O.C. ADMINISTRATIVE WARNING TO ARRESTEE
(To be given to any person exposed to O.C.)
A.

You have been contaminated with Oleoresin Capsicum (O.C.), this is a natural
product derived from Cayenne Peppers. I am going to treat you to reduce the
discomfort you are feeling, as long as you cooperate.

B.

O.C. is non-toxic and the effects will dissipate in a short time. The effects of O.C.
may however, mask or cover other medical conditions, including overdoses or
toxic levels of drugs like Cocaine, Amphetamines or alcohol

C.

I am going to ask you 5 questions for your own safety. Not answering my
questions withholding information or giving false or misleading answers could
delay medical treatment and may seriously jeopardize your health and safety.

Question #1
Are you currently under the influence of Cocaine, PCP, Heroin, Alcohol or any other
drug?_______ Which one(s)_______
Question#2
Have you taken Cocaine, Heroin, PCP or any other drug in the last 8 hours? _______
Which one(s)_______
Question #3
Do you normally take any illegal drugs or prescription drugs? _______
Which one(s)_______

Question #4
Do you have heart problems, lung problems, diabetes, high blood pressure or any other
serious medical conditions?_______ Which one(s)_______
Question #5
Do you have any allergies?_______ To what? _______
DID YOU ANSWER ALL QUESTIONS TRUTHFULLY? _______
X.

DECONTAMINATION AFTER THE USE OF O.C.
When a person has been sprayed with O.C. the officer(s) shall: (manufacturer's
recommendations are included in the following steps):
A.

Have the subject stay still and they should be told to breathe normally and relax as
much as possible. The subject should be moved into an uncontaminated area as
soon as possible and be faced into the wind. Fans can be used.

B.

If practical before transporting, cool water may be used to flush the subjects face
and eyes. A garden hose, kitchen sprayer, or hand held water sprayer work well.
DO NOT ALLOW THE SUBJECT TO RUB HIS/HER EYES. Special note:
Water will soothe the O.C., but will not in itself remove the resin from the skin.
Flushing the eyes may have to be repeated several times to remove the O.C.

C.

When the subject is no longer combative, the subject will be given copious
amounts of cold water to flush the face and eyes and other contaminated areas.
Subjects wearing contact lenses must remove them before flushing the eyes to
facilitate the decontamination process of their eyes. Later, they may then
thoroughly clean and soak the lenses with appropriate cleaning solutions. Most
soft lenses have to be discarded. Mild soap may also be provided to complete and
aid in the decontamination process. Do not use lotions, or creams on the affected
areas. These will trap the resin against the skin.

D.

When possible, transport the subject to the College Public Safety Office
immediately. During the transportation of the subject, the front windows of the
Public Safety vehicle shall be open to allow for a maximum amount of air flow to
the subject.

NOTE: During the summer months and/or warm weather, the Public Safety vehicle's air conditioner shall be turned on and put at its coldest setting, with the blower on high. Never place the subject on his/her stomach during transportation. This will avoid positional asphyxia.
A Peace Officer will remain with the subject until the effects of the O.C. reach a level where the subject can see.
If a subject is violent or threatening and where possible, the subject will be locked in a holding area with a bucket of cold water, and the bucket will be refilled with fresh water as needed.
Officers should be aware that not every person exposed to O.C. may be capable of self-decontamination and may require assistance in the process.

Use of a wet paper towel pressed on the face followed by a dry paper towel has proven to be the most effective way to remove the resin from the skin. Towels should be applied numerous times until the resin is removed.
Once this is done, again pat dry with a cloth or paper towels. DO NOT RUB.
Do not use any commercial eye wash during the decontamination process.

Under normal circumstances all major symptoms should disappear within 30 to 45 minutes If symptoms persist, seek medical attention immediately. If arrestee requests medical attention, it should be given.
If irritation persists, then seek medical attention for the subject.
DOCUMENTATION OF THE USE OF O.C.

In all cases where O.C. is unholstered or discharged by a University Peace Officer, a written Public Safety Incident Report and a Weapon Discharged/Use Report shall be prepared in accordance with The City University of New York Public Safety procedures. It shall be prepared and submitted to the Office of the University Public Safety Director with all relevant facts within 24 hours of the incident.

inst.title: Summary Penalties for Violations of Rules of Conduct
b: Below is a listing of Rules of Conduct, Operating Instruction (“O. I.”) No.11, the violation of which enables a College Public Safety Director to impose summary penalties without the filing of formal disciplinary charges. The University remains committed to progressive discipline and to full compliance with disciplinary procedures as set forth in the University’s Classified Staff Blue Collar Unit Collective Bargaining Agreement, except where the Union and the University have reached agreement as outlined below. All summary penalties must be documented on the attached form, reported to the University Director of Public Safety, and filed in the College Office of Human Resources. All officers shall have the right to have a union representative present during a summary penalty disciplinary conference. Documentation for all summary penalties imposed will be placed in the officer’s personnel file. The union will be provided with copies of any summary penalty discipline imposed by a college. Prior summary penalties for any offense may be introduced at subsequent disciplinary hearings.

These summary penalties apply to provisional, probationary, and permanent employees in campus security and/or campus peace officer titles. They do not, however, confer rights on provisional or probationary employees that they would otherwise not have. Summary penalties imposed by the College Public Safety Director, or his or her designee, the College Assistant Director of Public Safety for any Category “A” or “B” violation shall be subject to the existing Blue Collar grievance procedures, including using such procedures for provisional and probationary employees, except that use of such procedures by said employees shall apply only in the instance of summary penalties and shall not establish grievance rights for provisional and probationary employees where none otherwise existed. Consistent with Civil Service Law and University Policy, termination of provisional or probationary employees is not subject to the grievance or disciplinary procedure, except as provided in Article XXV, Section 1 (d) of the Blue Collar Agreement.

Any summary penalty sought to be imposed against a permanent officer or a provisional officer with contractual disciplinary rights for Category “C” or “D” violations will be subject to the officer’s “right of refusal.” If such officer refuses to accept the summary penalty, the College shall proceed to file formal disciplinary charges in accordance with the Blue Collar Agreement, which may result in the imposition of a more severe penalty. A probationary officer or provisional officer with no contractual disciplinary rights who refuses a summary penalty for a Category “C” or “D violation may be subject to immediate discharge.

These summary penalties do not limit the college’s discretionary authority to file formal disciplinary charges in lieu of seeking to impose summary penalties regarding any Category “A,” “B,” “C,” or “D” violation.
The imposition of a summary penalty will be imposed at the discretion of the College and will be based on the category of the specific violation, as follows:

Category “A” Violations: At the discretion of the College, forfeiture of up to three (3) annual or compensatory leave days, or suspension without pay for the remainder of the tour, or suspension without pay of up to three (3) work days, and/or a letter of reprimand to be placed in the officer’s personnel file, and/or the cost of replacing an officer’s Shield/I.D. if the officer failed to safeguard such;
Category “B” Violations: At the discretion of the College, forfeiture of up to ten (10) annual or compensatory leave days, or suspension without pay for up to ten (10) work days;
Category “C” Violations: At the discretion of the College, suspension without pay for up to thirty (30) calendar days; and

Category “D” Violations: At the discretion of the College, the penalty for Category “D” Violations shall include, but not be limited to, a suspension without pay for up to one hundred and twenty (120) calendar days; a six (6) months leave without pay, evidence of rehabilitation (if relevant), examination prior to return to duty (medical or psychological, if relevant), and a six (6) month probationary period upon return to duty.
It is agreed and understood that multiple summary penalties will not be imposed for the same occurrence.

Rule of Conduct: The loss of the shield or NYPD Peace Officer/CUNY public safety identification card shall be reported immediately by the officer by telephone, by the filing of a College Public Safety Incident Report and in person to the College Director of Public Safety and the University Director of Public Safety. In addition, the loss shall be reported at once to the jurisdiction of the Police Department in the area where the card or shield was believed to be lost (Ref. O. I. #1, Pg.2, ¶B3). Failure to report the loss of shield and I.D. card to the police department and to College/University Director of Public Safety constitutes a violation of this rule.
Violation: FAILURE TO SAFEGUARD SHIELD AND/OR I.D. CARD

Rule of Conduct: Sergeants, corporals and patrol officers on duty will be properly uniformed, neat and clean in their personal appearance. When wearing the police type uniform, the uniform hat may be left off while a member is operating a patrol vehicle, but must be worn immediately upon leaving the vehicle. The wearing of beards is prohibited. Mustaches shall be neatly trimmed. (See O. I. #5); and (Ref. O. I. #1, Pg. 2, B4)

Rule of Conduct: Sergeants, corporals and patrol officers in uniform (and/or in plain clothes) while on duty shall not enter any premises which are primarily used for the manufacture, storage, shipping, or sale of intoxicants, unless in the immediate performance of official patrol duty. (Ref. O. I. #1, Pg. 3, D13)
Violation: PRESENCE IN AN UNAUTHORIZED PREMISE

Rule of Conduct: All officers are required to report to work and remain on post as scheduled. All officers shall notify their commanding officer or College Public Safety Director or his/her designee of any request, emergency or other, to absent himself/herself from an assigned post and/or tour or patrol assignment. (Ref. O. I. # 1, Pg. 3, II. C. 1)
Violation: ABSENCE FROM POST AND/OR TOUR ASSIGNMENT WITHOUT AUTHORIZATION

Rule of Conduct: All officers are required to attend roll call at the designated place and time in order to receive instructions and any other special directives from their commanding officer before departing to their respective patrol/tour assignments. (Ref. O. I. #1, Pg. 3, II. A. 1; II. C. 1 and 2; )
Violation: FAILURE TO ATTEND ROLL CALL

Rule of Conduct: All officers are required to wear the proper college public safety uniform and to possess the proper designated equipment while on duty. (Ref. O.I. # 6, Pg. 2, III; and O.I. # 1, Pg. 3, II. D. 1)

Rule of Conduct: All officers are required to submit complete written or oral reports, including the completion of memorandum book entries, log book entries, etc., that are accurate as to facts following an investigation, interview, incident, complaint or other noteworthy event during the tour of duty. Such entries are deemed a business record created in the regular course of business. (Ref. O.I. #1, Pg. 1, II. A. 5; O. I. #12, Pg. 1, I; and Pg. 6, V. D. 1-5)
Violation: FAILURE TO COMPLETE A MEMORANDUM BOOK ENTRY OR LOG BOOK ENTRY FOLLOWING AN INVESTIGATION,
INTERVIEW, COMPLAINT, OR OTHER NOTEWORTHY EVENT DURING THE TOUR OF DUTY

Rule of Conduct: All officers are required to accurately make all required entries onto college records, forms and/or reports that may involve, inter alia, events, incidents and/or other situations occurring on campus requiring a written business record in the normal course of the officer’s duties. (Ref. O.I. #1, Pg. 1, II A 5)
Violation: FAILURE TO ACCURATELY MAKE ALL REQUIRED ENTRIES IN COLLEGE RECORDS, FORMS OR REPORTS

Rule of Conduct: All officers shall be responsible for submitting written or oral reports that are truthful and accurate as to facts in a timely manner (e.g., contemporaneous with the event, incident and/or occurrence.). (Ref. O.I. #1, Pg. 1, II. A. 5)
Violation: FAILURE TO SUBMIT REPORTS IN A TIMELY MANNER

Rule of Conduct: All officers must immediately notify his/her College Public Safety Director, Immediate Supervisor or University Public Safety Official (i.e., “Chain of Command”) of any incident affecting the effective administration of the campus safety operation. (Ref. O.I. #13, II. A-L)
Violation: FAILURE TO MAKE PROPER NOTIFICATIONS

Rule of Conduct: All officers in uniform and/or plain clothes shall not smoke while on duty, except in designated areas on campus during a meal break when the officer is off duty. (Ref. O.I. # 1. Pg. 3, II. D. 4)

Rule of Conduct: All officers shall be responsible for the good care, proper maintenance, serviceable condition and safeguarding of CUNY/College property, including vehicles, radios, keys, etc, issued or assigned for their use in the regular course of college business. All officers shall safeguard college equipment from loss, damage or theft. (See Ref. O.I. #1, Pg. 5, II. E. 1). Failure to adhere to the above rule of conduct will constitute a violation.
Violation: FAILURE TO SAFEGUARD COLLEGE PROPERTY
Rule of Conduct: All officers shall be punctual in reporting for duty on time and maintaining assigned work schedules. (Ref. O.I. # 1, Pg. 3, II. C. 2 - Revised See No. 14 below)

Rule of Conduct: All officers shall be responsible for reporting for duty as assigned, and shall not disrupt the security staffing assignments of the college public safety office due to excessive absences, which shall be defined as more than four (4) absences in a six-month period. (See, Ref. O.I. # 1, Pg. 3, II. C. 2 - Revised)

Rule of Conduct: All officers shall be civil and respectful to superior officers and designated University or College Officials, including, but not limited to, conducting themselves with dignity and courtesy at all times when in contact with members of the public/University community.. (Ref. O.I. # 1, Pg. 1, II. A. 2 and 3)
Violation: FAILURE TO BE CIVIL AND RESPECTFUL

Rule of Conduct: All officers are prohibited from engaging in conduct which may be disruptive, inappropriate, unprofessional, or detrimental to the performance of his/her duties as a campus peace officer or security officers. (Ref. O.I. # 1, Pg. 1, II. A. - new provision)
Violation: ENGAGING IN DISRUPTIVE, INAPPROPRIATE, UNPROFESSIONAL, OR DETRIMENTAL CONDUCT

Rule of Conduct: All officers must promptly obey all lawful orders and instructions, including, but not limited to, making routine inspection, properly performing tour/patrol assignments, surveys, etc. (Ref. O.I. # 1, Pg. 1, II. A. 1)
Violation: FAILURE TO MAKE ROUTINE INSPECTIONS, OR FAILURE TO PROPERLY PERFORM PATROL ASSIGNMENTS, OR SURVEYS AS REQUIRED

Rule of Conduct: Campus Public Safety Equipment, including, but not limited to, campus public safety vehicles, shall be issued only for official purposes and used for the purpose for which it is designated related to college business. Unauthorized personnel, staff, students or others (e.g., relatives, friends, etc.) are prohibited from riding in a College Public Safety Vehicle, unless in the regular course of college business, emergency, etc. Moreover, the equipment will be used only by the officer to whom it has been assigned, unless otherwise directed by a college public safety supervisor or higher authority. (Ref. O. I. # 1, Pg. 5, II. E. 3).
Violation: UNAUTHORIZED USE OF A COLLEGE PUBLIC SAFETY VEHICLE

Rule of Conduct: All officers shall be dignified and courteous in their dealings with other members of the service, University/College officials, staff or students, or members of the college community, which shall include providing the officers name, shield number, and rank upon request at all times. (Ref. O. I. # 1, Pg. 1, II. A. 3 and 4)
Violation: FAILURE TO GIVE NAME, SHIELD NUMBER AND RANK TO A COLLEGE OFFICIAL, FACULTY, STAFF, OR STUDENT

Rule of Conduct: All officers while on duty shall not carry any object which is not part of the designated uniform, and/or engage in reading or writing not related to University business or to the officer’s job assignment. An exception to this rule shall be when an officer aids a student (including those who are disabled/handicapped), faculty, staff, or a visitor to the college under certain circumstances, which may include, but is not limited to, the carrying of books, packages, equipment. (Ref. O.I. # 1, Pg. 3, II. D 1 and 2; and O.I. # 6)
Violation: CARRYING PACKAGES, NEWSPAPERS, BOOKS, EQUIPMENT OR OTHER ARTICLES NOT PART OF AN OFFICER’S ASSIGNED UNIFORM

Rule of Conduct: All officers are prohibited from using college equipment, e.g., telephones, computers, without the authorization of the College Public Safety Director or college official, which use shall be related to the officer’s assignment.
Violation: UNAUTHORIZED USE OF COLLEGE EQUIPMENT

Rule of Conduct: All officers assigned to operate a Campus Public Safety Vehicle or any other Official College Vehicle shall comply with all vehicle and traffic laws and regulations of the State of New York or other jurisdictions traveled to by an officer in furtherance of college business.
Violation: FAILURE TO COMPLY WITH VEHICLE AND TRAFFIC LAWS (VTL), WHILE DRIVING A COLLEGE VEHICLE

Rule of Conduct: All officers shall immediately report to the College Public Safety Director or his/her designee, the revocation and/or suspension of a NYS issued driver license. Any officer whose NYS driver license has been revoked or suspended will be prohibited from driving a Campus Public Safety Vehicle.
Violation: FAILURE TO REPORT THE REVOCATION OR SUSPENSION OF A NYS DRIVER’S LICENSE; AND/OR DRIVING A CAMPUS PUBLIC SAFETY VEHICLE WITH A REVOKED OR SUSPENDED NYS DRIVER’S LICENSE

Rule of Conduct: All officers shall place the University Memorandum Book in the authorized regulation leather memo book binder and have it on his/her person while on duty at all times. (O.I. # 12, Pg. 3, II. D 4)
Violation: LOSS OF UNIVERSITY MEMORANDUM BOOK OR FAILURE TO HAVE IT IN THE OFFICER’S POSSESSION WHILE ON DUTY

Rule of Conduct: All officers are prohibited from arriving or remaining on campus more than 60 minutes before or after a tour of duty without authorization of the College Public Safety Director or his/her designee. An exception to this rule of conduct shall be if the subject officer is a duly enrolled student of the College.
Violation: ARRIVING OR REMAINING ON CAMPUS FOR MORE THAN 60 MINUTES BEFORE OR AFTER A TOUR OF DUTY WITHOUT AUTHORIZATION OF THE COLLEGE PUBLIC SAFETY DIRECTOR OR HIS/HER DESIGNEE

Rule of Conduct: All officers shall aid or assist other members of the service when an officer is in need of assistance, including, but not limited to, processing and/or referring an officer’s request for temporary relief of their post.
Violation: FAILURE TO AID A FELLOW OFFICER OR TO PROCESS AND/OR REFER HIS/HER REQUEST FOR TEMPORARY RELIEF OF POST

Rule of Conduct: All officers intending to engage in any outside employment, shall first obtain joint approval from his/her College Public Safety Director and College Human Resource Director in compliance with CUNY’s Rules and Regulations 5.1.1, and Personnel Policy Bulletin 3-90 dated March 3, 1990. (Ref. O.I. #1 - Amend)
Violation: ENGAGING IN OUTSIDE EMPLOYMENT WITHOUT FIRST OBTAINING JOINT AUTHORIZATION FROM THE COLLEGE PUBLIC SAFETY DIRECTOR AND COLLEGE HUMAN RESOURCE DIRECTOR

Rule of Conduct: All officers shall be punctual in reporting for duty and maintaining assigned work schedules, notwithstanding any authorized outside employment. An exception shall be made if the officer receives prior joint approval from the College Public Safety Director and College Human Resource Director (Ref. O.I. #1 - Amend)
Violation: LATENESS IN ARRIVING AT AND/OR EARLY DEPARTURE FROM A TOUR OF DUTY OWING TO AUTHORIZED OUTSIDE EMPLOYMENT

Rule of Conduct: All officers while on duty shall not carry and/or use a cell phone or other electronic communications devices without the express authorization from the College Director of Public Safety for specific instances relating to college business. (Ref. O. I. # 1, Pg. 3, II. D. 1)
Violation: CARRYING AND/OR USING A CELL PHONE OR PAGER WHILE ON DUTY

Rule of Conduct: All officers must promptly obey all lawful and proper orders and instructions written or otherwise, however transmitted or received from their supervisor or University/College Official. This shall also include responding to a fellow officer’s radio call for relief, assistance, etc. (Ref. O. I. # 1, Pg. 1, II. A 1).
Violation: FAILURE TO RESPOND TO A FELLOW OFFICER’S RADIO CALL FOR RELIEF, ASSISTANCE, ETC.
Rule of Conduct: Sergeants, corporals and patrol officers shall not sleep during an assigned work tour. (Ref. O. I. #1, Pg. 3, D3)
Rule of Conduct: Sergeants, corporals and patrol officers shall not drink intoxicants while in uniform. (Ref. O. I. #1, Pg. 3, ¶D11)
Violation: CONSUMPTION OF INTOXICANTS WHILE IN UNIFORM

Rule of Conduct: All officers are prohibited from engaging in any activities not part of their assigned work duties, such as watching television or using any unauthorized electronic equipment, etc., on campus while on duty. (See, Ref. O.I. # 1, Pg. 3, II, D. 1)
Violation: WATCHING TELEVISION OR USING OTHER UNAUTHORIZED ELECTRONIC EQUIPMENT WHILE ON DUTY

Rule of Conduct: All officers are prohibited from occupying an unauthorized area of the college designated by a College Official/Administrator or the College Public Safety Director, unless the officer is given specific instructions by his/her superiors in the regular course of duty.
Violation: OCCUPYING AN UNAUTHORIZED AREA OF THE COLLEGE (E.G., A FACULTY OR ADMINISTRATIVE OFFICE) WHICH MAY INCLUDE LOUNGING, SLEEPING, USING COLLEGE TELEPHONES, ETC.

Rule of Conduct: All officers shall be honest, truthful, accurate and shall not engage in any unauthorized or misleading act, nor shall they make or submit any false or misleading written or oral statements. All officers shall comply with the college’s rules and regulations, including, but not limited to, the college’s parking policy and procedures and the use of parking permits/sticker. (Ref. O. I. #1, Pg. 1, II. A. 5)
Violation: NONCOMPLIANCE WITH COLLEGE PARKING POLICY, INCLUDING MISUSE OF PARKING PERMITS

Rule of Conduct: All officers shall provide truthful and accurate records of their time and leave, and shall make truthful and accurate entries of same. All officers shall comply with the college’s rules and regulations, including, but not limited to, complying with the college’s time and leave policies; ensuring that employees do not abuse or violate such rules; and refrain from aiding or abetting staff or others in the violation of same. (Ref. O. I. #1, Pg. 1, II. A. 5)
Violation: SIGNING, SWIPING OR OTHERWISE CERTIFYING “IN OR OUT” FOR ANOTHER OFFICER OR STAFF WITHOUT PERMISSION OF THE COLLEGE PUBLIC SAFETY DIRECTOR OR COLLEGE HUMAN RESOURCE DIRECTOR

Rule of Conduct: All officers shall not fraternize with students, staff or other officers, which act is unrelated to college business and/or not in furtherance of their security assignment. (See, Ref. O. I. # 1, Pg. 4, II. D.10)
Violation: FRATERNIZING WITH STUDENTS, STAFF OR OTHER OFFICERS WHILE ON DUTY
Rule of Conduct: All officers shall report to the College Public Safety Director any traffic violation in which a fine and/or moving violation points were assessed and paid for by the officer.
Violation: FAILURE TO REPORT A TRAFFIC VIOLATION IN WHICH A FINE AND/OR MOVING VIOLATION POINTS WERE ASSESSED

Rule of Conduct: Following a letter of reprimand or penalty in Category “A,” an officer continues secondary employment without joint authorization of the College Public Safety Director and College Director of Human Resources.
Violation: CONTINUED FAILURE TO OBTAIN JOINT AUTHORIZATION OF THE COLLEGE PUBLIC SAFETY DIRECTOR AND COLLEGE HUMAN RESOURCE DIRECTOR FOR OUTSIDE EMPLOYMENT

Rule of Conduct: Any violation in Category “A” for which there is a second occurrence, and for which the College elects not to pursue disciplinary action under the University’s Blue Collar Collective Bargaining Agreement, will result in a Category “B” penalty of up to a 10 work day suspension without pay, or the forfeiture of 10 annual or compensatory leave days.

Rule of Conduct: Sergeants, corporals and officers who have been designated by the president of the college to bear arms and those officers who have not been designated to bear arms shall never brandish any weapons, nor shall they remove arms or weapons from holders or holsters, other than in the proper performance of duty. (Ref. O. I. #1, Pg 4, D15; and O.I. # 3, Pg. 1, 1)

Note: In the event an officer (1) improperly displays an authorized fire arm under his/her control, or (2) improperly displays and/or uses a weapon other than a fire arm, in addition to the summary penalties provided herein, such will result in the immediate removal of the officer’s fire arms bearing designation, and discontinuation of his/her fire arms differential pay. Upon the employee's return from suspension, restoration to the fire arms bearing designation may be made only upon recommendation of the College Director of Public Safety and with approval of the University Director of Public Safety. For subsequent offenses, the employee shall be subject to formal disciplinary procedures.
Violation: IMPROPER DISPLAY AND/OR USE OF A FIRE ARM OR ANY OTHER WEAPON
Rule of Conduct: When a sergeant, corporal or officer is apparently unfit for duty due to intoxication or being under the influence of drugs, a ranking officer shall take the following action:
If the sergeant, corporal or officer is reporting for duty, not permit him/her to perform duty.
If the sergeant, corporal or officer is on duty, relieve him/her from duty. (Ref. O. I. #1, Pg. 3, D12).
Note: In addition to the summary penalties provided herein, the College Director of Public Safety may require the employee to submit to immediate drug testing in

accordance with the University Reasonable Suspicion Policy. For subsequent offenses the employee shall be subject to formal disciplinary procedures and must be required to go for immediate drug testing. Drug tests are administered by providers who hold contracts with the University and conducted in accordance with the procedures covered under the University Reasonable Suspicion Policy.
Violation: UNFIT FOR DUTY DUE TO INTOXICATION OR BEING UNDER THE INFLUENCE OF DRUGS

Rule of Conduct: All officers are prohibited from driving while intoxicated or driving without a valid license issued by the State of New York. Moreover, all officers shall comply with the NYS Vehicle and Traffic Laws (VTL) and other laws within the State of New York and surrounding jurisdictions.
Violation: ANY ARREST FOR “DWI” OR “DWL” FOR WHICH A BADGE/ SPECIAL PATROLMAN STATUS IS NOT REVOKED/REMOVED AS A RESULT OF THE INCIDENT

Rule of Conduct: All officers are prohibited from using sexually provocative language or engaging in sexually provocative behavior on campus while in or out of uniform. Such conduct would be inappropriate even if consensual and/or it did not result in the filing of a complaint under the University’s Sexual Harassment Policy and Procedures.

Note: When a complaint has been filed under the University’s Sexual Harassment Policy and Procedures, it will be handled in accordance with those procedures and may result in the filing of formal disciplinary charges.
Violation: USING SEXUALLY PROVOCATIVE LANGUAGE OR ENGAGING IN SEXUALLY PROVOCATIVE BEHAVIOR ON CAMPUS, WHILE IN OR OUT OF UNIFORM

Rule of Conduct: All officers shall cooperate in all investigations conducted by a duly appointed investigatory body or official of the College or University, except as may be protected by law. All officers shall provide truthful accurate statements of the facts and shall not misstate the facts, give misleading information or provide incomplete information during said investigation pertaining to another officer’s behavior or other matter at the college, to a duly appointed investigatory body or official of the College or University. (Ref. O. I. #1, Pg. 1, A - New)
Violation: REFUSING TO COOPERATE IN AN OFFICIAL INVESTI- GATION AND/OR LYING, MISSTATING THE FACTS, GIVING INCOMPLETE INFORMATION IN THE COURSE OF THE INVESTIGATION

Rule of Conduct: All officers must promptly obey all lawful orders and instructions, written or otherwise, however, transmitted or received, from their supervisors, including, but not limited to, the president and vice president of a college to which the officer is assigned. (Ref. O. I. #1, Pg. 1, A1)
Violation: REFUSING TO OBEY A LAWFUL ORDER AND/OR INSTRUCTIONS; INSUBORDINATION

Rule of Conduct: Any offense in Category “B” for which there is a second occurrence or any offense in Category “A” for which there is a third occurrence, and for which the College elects not to pursue disciplinary action under the University’s Blue Collar Collective Bargaining Agreement, will result in a Category “C” penalty of up to a thirty (30) calendar day suspension without pay.
Violation: SECOND CATEGORY “B” VIOLATION OR THIRD CATEGORY “A” VIOLATION

Rule of Conduct: Sergeants, corporals and officers shall not possess and/or use any unlawful intoxicants in any form (i.e., marijuana, heroin, cocaine, etc.) Furthermore, they shall not use any controlled substance without medical authorization and notification to the College Public Safety Director. Sergeants, Corporals, and officers shall not bring, permit to be brought, nor cause to be brought to a college or university facility, any controlled substance without medical authorization and notification to the College Public Safety Director. Sergeants, Corporals, and officers shall not bring, permit to be brought, nor cause to be brought, any unlawful intoxicants or non-authorized lawful intoxicants into a college or university facility.

Note: In the event of an egregious violation, an officer will be immediately suspended without pay and may be subject to possible arrest. The officer may also be subject to immediate drug testing in accordance with the University Reasonable Suspicion Policy.
Violation: UNAUTHORIZED POSSESSION AND/OR USE OF A CONTROLLED SUBSTANCE OR POSSESSION AND/OR USE OF UNLAWFUL INTOXICANT

Rule of Conduct: All officers are prohibited from serving alcoholic beverages to students or drinking alcoholic beverages while on duty, except at an authorized event of the college and with the express permission of the College Public Safety Director. Moreover, all officers are prohibited from driving a college public safety vehicle while having consumed alcoholic beverages or while intoxicated. In the aforementioned event, the officer in question will be subject to a breath analysis test for alcohol. Failure to pass the breath analysis test or refusal to take the test, will subject the officer to the maximum summary penalty for a Category “C” Violation in the discretion of the College Public Safety Director. (Ref. O. I. #1, Pg. 4, II. D. 11 & 3).

Violation: UNAUTHORIZED SERVING OF ALCOHOLIC BEVERAGES TO STUDENTS; OR DRINKING ALCOHOLIC BEVERAGES WHILE ON DUTY; OR ATTEMPTING TO DRIVE A COLLEGE PUBLIC SAFETY VEHICLE WHILE INTOXICATED OR HAVING CONSUMED ALCOHOLIC BEVERAGES; OR FAILURE TO PASS OR REFUSAL TO TAKE A BREATH ANALYSIS TEST FOR ALCOHOL

Rule of Conduct: All officers are prohibited from accepting any awards, gifts, services, gratuities, or any article of value, in connection with the performance of their official duties, or in exchange for not enforcing a college or University policy, rule or regulation in the course of their official duties. An exception to this rule shall be any awards, etc., that are conveyed to an officer by the college or University in accordance with University policies, rules or regulation. (Ref. O. I. #1, Pg. 3, II. D. 7)

Violation: ACCEPTING ANY AWARD, GIFT, SERVICE, ETC., IN CONNECTION WITH THE PERFORMANCE OF AN OFFICER’S OFFICIAL DUTIES, OR IN EXCHANGE FOR NOT ENFORCING A COLLEGE OR UNIVERSITY POLICY, RULE OR REGULATION

Rule of Conduct: All officers shall immediately respond to an emergency request or call by another officer or by a person on campus with an emergency, unless relieved of such duty and given alternate instructions by a supervising or commanding officer. (Ref. O. I. # 1, Pg. 1, A - New)
Violation: FAILURE TO RESPOND TO AN EMERGENCY REQUEST/CALL FOR ASSISTANCE

Rule of Conduct: All officers shall be dignified and courteous in their dealings with other members of the college security force and all other employees and students of the University. All officers are prohibited from engaging in a physical altercation with staff, student or members of the college community, or another officer. The latter of which may include, but not be limited to, any physical contact, threatening another officer, or damaging another officer’s property or locker, whether on or off duty or on or off campus. (Ref. O. I. # 1, Pg. 1, II. A. 2. and 3; Also see, O.I. #1, Pg. 2, II. A. 8).

Violation: ENGAGING IN A PHYSICAL ALTERCATION WITH STAFF, STUDENTS, MEMBERS OF THE COLLEGE COMMUNITY OR ANOTHER OFFICER, INCLUDING THREATENING OR DAMAGING PERSONAL PROPERTY OR ASSIGNED COLLEGE EQUIPMENT OR PROPERTY, EITHER ON OR OFF DUTY OR ON OR OFF CAMPUS

Rule of Conduct: Any offense in Category “C” for which there is a second occurrence or any offense in Category “B” for which there is a third occurrence, and for which the College elects not to pursue disciplinary action under the University’s Blue Collar Collective Bargaining Agreement, will result in a Category “D” penalty of up to a one-hundred and twenty (120) calendar day suspension without pay.
Violation: SECOND CATEGORY “C” VIOLATION OR THIRD CATEGORY “B” VIOLATION

These policies have been formulated within the scope and intent of the University Public Safety Initiative. Failure to comply with these policies, instructions and guidelines may result in a recommendation to appropriate college officials that disciplinary charges be filed.

The City University of New York Memorandum Book (UMB) is intended to serve as a logbook, memory aid and as protection against false accusations made against University Public Safety Personnel. As such, it must be accurately maintained in order to be of greatest value. All members of the University Public Safety Department covered under Campus Public Safety titles (uniformed members of service) assigned to shift coverage will routinely prepare the U.M.B. each day and follow the prescribed methodology in this instruction.

The guidelines listed below have been developed to assist officers in tracking and recording daily activity and individual responses to calls for assistance. It is imperative that each officer properly store and safeguard the completed U.M.B. as this record may be subject to subpoena in future criminal, civil or disciplinary proceedings. inst.title: Public Safety Notifications
b: This instruction prescribes The City University of New York policies for public safety notifications as set forth by the University Director of Public Safety for the effective administration of campus public safety operations.

These policies have been formulated within the scope and intent of the University’s Public Safety Initiative. Failure to comply with these policies, instructions and guidelines may result in a recommendation to appropriate college officials that disciplinary charges be filed.
The University Public Safety Director and respective Public Safety Borough Coordinators must be notified immediately whenever an incident at a CUNY college falls within the following categories:
Death Death of any person on campus property.
Serious Injury Serious injury to any person on campus property as a result of robbery or assault, where the injured person is hospitalized or where injury poses a threat to the injured’s life.
Robbery All robbery incidents (armed or strong-arm).
Sexual Assault/Rape All reported rape incidents or incidents of sexual assault on campus.
Chemical/Environmental Serious toxic spills or fires.
Property Damage Extensive college property damage.

Police or Fire Response to Campuses Notify the University Director of Public Safety immediately whenever there is an NYPD, FDNY or any other sworn law enforcement response to a CUNY college or property for reasons including but not limited to arrests, aided cases, bomb scares, evacuations, 911, disturbance, riot, 10-13 (assist patrolman) or fight-in- progress calls.
Arrests On-campus arrests of any CUNY student, employee, and faculty or staff member by any sworn law enforcement officer.
Activities Any college activity that could potentially impact on public safety or merit a heightened sense of public safety.
Significant Incident Any incident that could potentially expose the university to litigation or be reflected in the media due to the nature of the circumstances involved.
NOTE: Members of the Public Safety Department must also make notifications to their immediate campus supervisors, directors and appropriate college officials, should any of the above occur.

inst.title: Private Security Policy
b: This instruction prescribes The City University of New York Policies for private security as set forth by the Board of Trustees*.
These policies are consistent with the scope and intent of the University’s Public Safety Initiative.
It is the policy of The City University of New York that all security and public safety services provided on college-owned or leased facilities shall be the responsibility of the college president.

College responsibility for public safety applies to any building or property owned or controlled by the college and used by the college in direct support of, or related to its educational purposes, and any building or property owned or controlled by a student organization recognized by the college. This includes student union buildings and other entities that bear the name of the college.

All public safety or public safety related functions at events in college facilities, such as performances, speeches, conferences, meetings, classes, and other special events shall be managed by the college. No private security personnel, such as bodyguards or escorts acting in a security capacity, with the exception of security guards contracted by the college, shall perform any campus security or security related functions. The use of armed private security guards is prohibited.

After consultation with the campus faculty and student constituencies, as well as the appropriate University offices, the colleges are to establish security and safety guidelines for persons or organizations appearing at campus events or using campus facilities consistent with this policy. Contracts for speaker or space rentals should contain conditions whereby events may be canceled or payments or deposits may be forfeited for failure to comply with college public safety policies and procedures. Additionally, any person or organization violating such an agreement may be denied future access to any
CUNY campus or related facility in addition to any other applicable college or lawful sanction.

This policy does not apply to federal, state, county or municipal sworn law enforcement officers or to foreign or international law enforcement personnel who are officially charged with the responsibility of providing security for particular individuals, or who are involved in a law enforcement capacity (e.g. crowd control), in conjunction with the public safety officers of the college.

This general policy clarifies and subsumes security policies contained in the Henderson Rules and the CUNY Manual of General Policy (group that do not comply with college or University Public Safety shall be denied access to college facilities) and the University Fiscal Handbook (there shall be no frisking or searches, except by sworn law enforcement officers). This policy, which applies to all facilities and events whether fees are paid to speaker or funded through student fees, is not intended to limit or abridge individual access to or attendance at college events

In the event that private security is necessary and requires an exception to this policy, such exceptions must be approved by the college president and the chancellor, and reported to the Board of Trustees Committee on Fiscal Affairs at the earliest practicable time.
* Board of Trustees Meeting- March 21, 1994 Substitute Resolution Calendar No. 5 K. City University of New York- Private Security Policy

inst.title: Off-Duty Arrest Guidelines for University Peace Officers
b: The purpose of this instruction is to provide guidelines for University peace officers regarding acceptable criteria for effecting off-duty arrests and to clarify the 24 hour Peace Officer authority of CUNY officers which was signed into law on August 2, 1994. This instruction is promulgated by the University Director of Public Safety for the effective administration of campus public safety operations.

These instructions have been formulated within the scope and intent of the University Public Safety Initiative. Failure to comply with these policies, instructions and guidelines may result in a recommendation to appropriate college officials that disciplinary charges be filed.

The City University of New York recognizes that off-duty CUNY peace officers may be faced with situations involving criminal conduct or volatile confrontations wherein they must take enforcement action. Off-duty peace officers are generally at a disadvantage when making arrests, particularly during violent situations that may develop spontaneously in their presence. Such situations are difficult for most uniformed officers who are accustomed to responding to calls for service in which they frequently have time to prepare strategically and mentally for the encounter and can readily call for assistance. Moreover, the appearance of a uniformed officer often in and of itself helps to calm and diffuse potentially violent situations. In many cases, off-duty officers who are trained in observation and identification skills can render more help by using these skills to record and report rather than attempting to make an arrest under dangerous or unknown circumstances.

Placing limitations on the off-duty arrest powers of officers is a prudent means of minimizing the dangers inherent to most off-duty arrest scenarios. In vesting University peace officers with the lawful authority to make arrests to protect the public welfare, a careful balancing of all human interests is required. Off-duty arrests may lead to unnecessary injuries to off-duty officers, and confusion for on-duty law enforcement personnel arriving at the scene and trying to correctly assess the facts.

In order to promote safety for all parties involved, The City University of New York has established this policy to regulate those situations and determine the locations and circumstances, consistent with state law within which sworn members of the service are permitted to make arrests while off-duty.

Off- Duty Arrest Powers CUNY peace officers have the legal authority to make off duty arrests in accordance with Section 2.20 (1) (a) of the Criminal Procedure Law and Section 140.25 of the Criminal Procedure Law. Under Section 140.25 (4) of the Criminal Procedure Law a peace officer may anywhere in the state, arrest a person for a felony he has reasonable cause to believe that such person has committed in his presence, provided that the arrest is made during or immediately after the alleged criminal conduct or during the alleged perpetrator's immediate flight therefrom.

Section 140.25 of the CPL also sets forth another category of arrests which a peace officer may make, while off-duty. Pursuant to Section 140.25(3), a peace officer may arrest a person for an offense committed or believed by him to have been committed within the geographical area of the peace officer's employment (NYC) as follows:
He may arrest such person for any offense where such person has in fact committed such offense in his presence; and
He may arrest such person for a felony when he has reasonable cause to believe that such person has committed such felony, whether in his presence or otherwise.
Permitted Off-Duty Arrests When off-duty and within the legal jurisdiction of the University Public Safety Department (NYC), a University peace officer may make an arrest only when:

The arresting officer is not personally involved in the incident underlying the arrest. Personally involved means where the off-duty officer, a family member, or a friend becomes engaged in a dispute or incident with the person to be arrested or any other person connected with the incident. This does not apply to situations where the peace officer himself is a victim of crime; or
There is an immediate need for the prevention of a crime or apprehension of a suspect; or
The crime would be charged as a jailable offense requiring a full custodial arrest; or
The arresting peace officer is in possession of appropriate peace officer identification. (Shield and I.D. Card)
Off-Duty Arrests - Restrictions It is the policy of the CUNY Public Safety Department that University Peace Officers not make off-duty arrests in the following situations:
When the arresting officer is personally involved in the incident underlying the arrest; or
When engaged in off-duty employment and the officer's actions are only in furtherance of the interests to the private employer; or
When the arrest is made solely as enforcement of a minor traffic regulation. (i.e. stop sign, red light, parking etc.) or

When the arrest is to enforce offenses or minor violations such as harassment, disorderly conduct or other quality-of-life offenses. On-duty police personnel should be contacted to respond to the situation where an off-duty peace officer becomes aware of such violations.

Notification of Off-Duty Arrests and Documentation of Arrests In any cases where a University peace officer has effected an off-duty arrest, the arresting officer will immediately thereafter notify his/her respective College Public Safety Director and prepare a written Public Safety Incident Report detailing all relevant facts surrounding the arrest within 24 hours. A copy of the completed Public Safety Incident Report will be forwarded to the Office of the University Public Safety Director.

Off-Duty Arrest Compensation CUNY peace officers making off duty arrests shall be allotted 4 hours to process the arrest and 8 hours to appear at any subsequent court or preparatory administrative meeting. (One occasion only)
While off-duty, it is the responsibility of the University peace officer to report any suspected or observed criminal activities to on-duty police authorities as soon as possible.
Where an arrest is necessary, the off-duty arresting officer shall abide by all CUNY Public Safety policies and procedures.

Authorized Equipment CUNY peace officers have been trained in the use of and are authorized to carry handcuffs, the "ASP" retractable baton, and defensive cayenne pepper spray canisters while on duty. A small contingent of officers has also been authorized by their college president to carry service firearms while working.

Off duty, City University of New York peace officers are only authorized to carry or possess handcuffs. The possession, while off duty, of firearms, baton (ASP) or pepper spray issued by the University is prohibited. CUNY peace officers owning or carrying personal firearms by virtue of having been appropriately licensed to do so by a governmental agency are not to carry said firearms on CUNY college campuses unless specifically authorized to do so by the college presidents. Only CUNY peace officers are authorized to carry University issued firearms while on duty pursuant to the authorization of their college president, and upon successful completion of New York State Division of Criminal Justice Services mandated firearms training.

Liability/Indemnification Issues University peace officers of the University Public Safety Department have liability protection for the on-and off-duty performance of official duties. This protection does not extend to willful acts to cause injury or damage, or to those actions that the peace officer knew, or reasonably should have known, were in conflict with law, or the established policies or customs of the University Public Safety Department. Specifically CUNY officers making arrests while off-campus and off-duty will be indemnified by the State or City against claims such as false arrest or brutality. Section 2.20 (3) of the Criminal Procedure Law provides that a peace officer, whether or not acting pursuant to his special duties, who lawfully exercises any of the powers conferred upon him pursuant to Section 2.20, shall be deemed to be acting within the scope of his public employment for purposes of defense and indemnification rights under Section 17 of the Public Officers Law which is applicable to state employees) and Section 50K of the General Municipal Law (applicable to city employees). Accordingly, the CUNY officers would be indemnified, even for off-duty and off-campus conduct, provided that they are lawfully exercising their powers of arrest as set forth in Section 140.25 of the Criminal Procedure Law.

inst.title: Inspections Policy & Procedure [Uniforms/Field]
b: This instruction outlines The City University of New York Public Safety Department procedure for the inspection of College Public Safety Departments including the inspection of uniforms. This Policy has been formulated within the scope and intent of the University Public Safety Initiative. Failure to comply with these policies, instructions and guidelines may result in a recommendation to appropriate college officials that disciplinary charges be filed.

The purpose of the inspections program is to ensure that uniforms and equipment worn by members of the CUNY Public Safety Department meet the specifications and directives established by The University Director of Public Safety and document the replacement of uniforms and equipment no longer serviceable.

Similarly, consistent with the system-wide public safety audit responsibility of the Office of the University Director of Public Safety, these inspections will ensure that personnel, and the physical condition of the College Public Safety Offices, equipment and operating procedures of the respective college Public Safety Units are examined to determine if the University’s Public Safety Initiative objectives are being met accordance with existing administrative standards, policies and procedures.
There are three (3) general categories of inspections:

Local College Inspections These inspections are staff functions which are assigned by the College Director of Public Safety and should be conducted on a daily basis during roll call. Supervisory personnel who are responsible for line personnel or assigned to direct the patrol functions of Public Safety personnel should perform this task. The purpose of these inspections is to ensure that officers are properly uniformed, equipped and fit for duty.

Unannounced Inspections Unannounced inspections should be conducted by the college Director of Public Safety and will also be conducted by the deputy University Director of Public Safety or his designee on an irregular basis (nights, weekends, holidays, etc.) to
determine if there is compliance with existing operational procedures, rules and regulations.

University Public Safety Inspections (Audits) These are periodic scheduled and announced college public safety inspections covering the complete range of public safety activities conducted by the University Director of Public Safety. College Supervisors assigned to staff administrative functions i.e., training, bicycle patrol, crime prevention, etc. will be asked to submit reports during staff inspections.
The principal areas to be reviewed during University Public Safety inspections are as follows:

Morale This area measures the ability to instill in subordinates a sense of professionalism, loyalty, dedication to duty and willingness to accept responsibility. Judgment, job knowledge, poise, initiative, decision making and officer enthusiasm are some of the specific characteristics observed and measured.

Quality of Supervision The supervisor’s ability to have orders promptly obeyed, the quality of reports submitted by both the supervisor and subordinates, the patrol function of the supervisor, preparation of complaints and commendations, and the response to incidents come under review.
Personal Appearance Adherence by college uniformed officers to the uniform and equipment standards specified in Operations Instruction #6 is reviewed and documented.
Supervisory Complaints Review local supervisory complaint reports and the corrective measures taken to prevent reoccurrences.

Civilian Complaints Determine the number and type of civilian complaints filed against members of the college Public Safety Departments during a specific period. Review the type of follow-up investigations conducted and the type of corrective taken, if warranted.
Records Evaluate condition and maintenance records of public safety department equipment issued to officers.
Safety Review motor vehicle accident reports, officer injury reports and safety training programs developed to reduce incident rates.

Enforcement Activity The number and types of enforcement actions taken, i.e. arrests, summonses in the form of Desk Appearance Tickets, if issued by N.Y.P.D., or any actions referred to college disciplinary boards for the reporting year are recorded.

Traffic Control Assess and evaluate the College Public Safety Department effectiveness in handling traffic congestion at college; the use of selective enforcement to reduce violations or the use of traffic control devices and/or markings.

Central Public Safety Command (college level) The neatness, cleanliness and operational effectiveness of the college Public Safety office, communications station, locker rooms and administrative offices is monitored and rated.
Training College instituted training programs are evaluated for their effectiveness and current applicability.
Emergency Plans The emergency plans of the college and their availability as well as the familiarity of public safety personnel with the plans will be reviewed.

Seasonal Inspections Inspection of uniforms, other than at daily roll call, shall be held at the beginning of each “uniform” season (Fall/Winter-Spring/Summer). Members of the Public Safety Department standing inspection will wear prescribed uniform for inspection in accordance with O.I. #6. A NYS Driver’s license is considered part of the uniform and must be submitted to the inspection team upon demand. All licenses are verified by the Office of the University director of Public Safety. The dates and description of uniform inspections are ad follows:

April and May (each year) Summer and spring uniform inspection: Summer uniforms (blouse and pants), summer shirts (long and short sleeve), hats (police type & baseball cap) car jacket, rain goods authorized shoes and leather goods.

September and October (each year) Fall and winter uniform inspection: Winter overcoat, car jacket, shirt, tie, and tie clasp, authorized shoes, pants, turtle neck sweater, hat (police type), commando sweater, and leather goods.

NOTE: During each uniform inspection and where applicable, a service firearm inspection will be conducted. Cleanliness and proper mechanical operation will be checked, however, firearms will never be discharged during these inspections. Service firearms which are found to be defective and cannot be repaired immediately will be confiscated by the inspecting officer. The inspecting officer will arrange for the repair and return of the firearm to the officer.

Report The Deputy University director of Public /safety is responsible for the submission of college inspection reports. After reviewing the results gathered by other members of the inspection team (staff officers assigned to the Office of the University Director of Public Safety), a detailed report will be forwarded to the President, Vice President, Director of Public Safety of the inspected college. The University director of Public Safety will also be notified of the inspection results.

Ratings Overall College Public Safety Department performances will be rated. The ratings will range from “unacceptable” to “outstanding” with recommendations for improvements provided in the “marginal” and “unacceptable” areas.

Corrective Measures Members of the College Public Safety Departments required to repair or replace uniform items must submit the items (see “Uniform Inspection follow-up Sheet”) for re-inspection to the College Director of Public Safety when repair or replacement has been affected. Item (s) will be submitted for re-inspection no later than three (3) weeks from the date of original inspection.

inst.title: Overtime Reporting Policy & Procedure
b: This instruction prescribes The City University of New York Public Safety policy for reporting overtime for University Officers (Sergeants, Corporals and Patrol Officers) as set forth by the University Director of Public Safety for the effective administration of campus public safety operations. This instruction establishes the necessary guidelines to accurately compensate uniformed members of the Public Safety Department who perform in excess of the hours stipulated in the member's regular work schedule. The University Public Safety Department Overtime Form (CUNY/UPS.1) is to be utilized or overtime performed at a site other than the officer=s assigned college.

When a member of The City University Public Safety Department, as defined in the policy statement, performs overtime duty, the member will submit the CUNY/UPS1 to his/her supervisor on duty. All entries will be accurate and complete. A concise description of the assigned overtime will include the date, location, and specific event. inst.title: Use of ASP [Collapsible] Baton
b: The City University of New York recognizes and respects the value and special integrity of each human life. In vesting University Peace Officers with the lawful authority to use force to protect the public welfare, a careful balancing of all human interests is required. The ability to use force is the primary factor which distinguishes the law enforcement community from the remainder of the society it serves. No other segment of society is permitted this license. As a result of this responsibility, the use of force by public safety personnel comes under close scrutiny by both the public and the courts.

This instruction prescribes The City University of New York policies for the use of The ASP collapsible baton as set forth by the University Director of Public Safety for the effective administration of campus public safety operations.

These policies have been formulated within the scope and intent of the University Public Safety Initiative. Violation of any of these policies may result in a recommendation that appropriate disciplinary action be taken against the officer violating said policy.

It is the policy of this University that its Peace Officers shall use only that force which is reasonably necessary to effectively protect the lives of the officer or another. A variety of options are available to University Peace Officers during confrontational settings. These are often referred to as the "force continuum". Techniques range from verbal persuasion or coercion, to hand control procedures such as escort pain/pressure compliance holds, or the use of more aggressive measures involving O.C. pepper spray or the ASP baton.

Every effort should be made to use verbal commands to compel the offender to follow the directions of the University Peace Officer. The most basic defensive measure available to an officer is the use of dialogue to persuade a subject to cooperate. "Talking" a subject into compliance avoids the inherent dangers of a physical confrontation in which the officer or subject may be injured. However, if dialogue is not effective, the next means of gaining control is the use of an escort technique. This is a low level compliance procedure, non-threatening and non-violent. The purpose of escort compliance is to remove an individual

from an area that may cause jeopardy to an individual or the officer. From a physical standpoint, escort is perhaps the most commonly employed technique used by law enforcement personnel. In those circumstances in which escort is inappropriate or ineffective but where higher use of force is not justified, pain compliance is appropriate and often extremely effective. Pain compliance should be used during circumstances wherein it would be too dangerous to merely escort an individual. During those occasions wherein verbal communication and escort techniques and the use of pepper spray fails or would be inappropriate, due to the officer's efforts being met with physical resistance or the threat of physical resistance, and the use of force is justified in accordance with the Penal code and Criminal Procedure Law of the State of New York, an impact weapon may be used to prevent/end the threat or effect an arrest. The use of the ASP baton constitutes a use of force which is not intended to be deadly physical force. Use of the ASP baton is authorized only in those instances and under such circumstances as authorized by law pursuant to Article 35 of the Penal Law of the State of New York. Force must cease when control has been effected. The use of force on an individual who is already under control is deemed punishment and exceeds the bounds of all prevailing standards of law enforcement conduct and will not be tolerated. Officers authorized by law to use force may be held both criminally and civilly liable for any inappropriate or excessive actions.

The ASP baton is a defensive, law enforcement impact weapon designed to be inconspicuous yet highly effective in an operational setting. The concealable nature of the baton makes it an ideal intermediate defensive option for the public safety officer. The ASP Baton is composed of the following:
Shaft composed of the mid-section and end-section.
Retaining spring, securing the shaft in the handle.
The ASP baton will be carried in the leather scabbard with which it was issued. These carriers provide positive retention while at the same time allowing rapid presentation of the baton.
All University Peace Officers must attend a certified training session approved by The City University of New York before being permitted to carry or use the ASP baton on duty.
University Peace Officers are authorized to carry the ASP Baton and must take part in all phases of the training in order to be certified.
University Peace Officers are not permitted the use of the ASP baton unless qualified in its proficient use as determined by established training procedures.
Parameters for use of The ASP baton:

The ASP baton will be used only after every effort has been made to use verbal commands to compel the offender to follow the directions of the University Peace Officer and the use of O.C. spray is not feasible or ineffective. If verbal commands are met with physical resistance or the threat of physical resistance, the use of O.C. spray as enumerated in Operations Instruction #10 (revised May 1995) should be considered if appropriate. The use of force must be justified as per the New York State Penal Law, Article 35 prior to employing the ASP Baton.

Where deadly physical force is not authorized, officers should assess the incident in order to determine which non-deadly technique or weapon will best de-escalate the incident and bring it under control in a safe manner and to accomplish a lawful task.
University Peace Officers are authorized to use department-approved non-deadly force techniques and are issued equipment for resolution of incidents, as follows:
In self-defense or the defense of others.
To control and effect an unlawful situation safely and effectively, and arrest an offender when physical force is justified under law and City University guidelines.
To assist in taking control of a violent, emotionally disturbed person (E.D.P.) who is a danger to himself or others.
When lower levels of force are deemed ineffective.
There are three primary target areas on the body:
The following areas should not be intended as targets:
The face. D. Spine. G. Internal Organs (liver, kidney, etc.)

Strikes to the face, head, neck, spine, sternum, groin and internal organs may produce injuries which could prove fatal. Strikes to the primary target areas (center mass of the arm, center mass of the leg, & the abdomen) have a high potential for control and a low potential for fatal injury. These targets are also "forgiving" targets. If the assailant moves or a strike misses its intended target, surrounding targets also have a high potential for control and a lesser potential for damage.
USE WITH VIOLENT EMOTIONALLY DISTURBED PERSON (E.D.P.'S)
An attempt should be made to calm the E.D.P, through reasoning and verbal persuasion whenever possible.

Whenever an officer (s) is confronted with a violent E.D.P, and the use of O.C. spray is not feasible or is ineffective upon the subject, the ASP baton may be used if the circumstances are such that attempts at other forms of physical restraint will likely result in injury to the subject or the officer (s).

When an E.D.P. is violent, threatening or armed with a dangerous instrument/weapons, O.C. spray, or if tactically feasible, the ASP baton may be used immediately to disarm and take control of the subject.

Upon issue by The City University of New York only qualified and authorized sworn Peace Officers shall carry the ASP baton. The device will be stored in its issued scabbard at all times. Any time the device is used, a Public Safety Incident Report will be filed and The University Public Safety Director and College Public Safety Director will be notified. The ASP baton will be carried only when on duty. When an officer is off duty, it will be stored in his or her locker. It will be the responsibility of the individual officer to keep the ASP Baton safe and within his/her control while on duty. Any ASP baton that is lost or stolen will be reported immediately to the on duty supervisor and a Command Log entry will be made. All ASP batons shall remain The City University of New York property and administrative control over them will be maintained by the University Director of Public Safety and his staff. In the event of loss, ASP batons will be replaced at the officer's expense.
DOCUMENTATION OF THE USE OF THE ASP BATON

In all cases where the ASP baton is unholstered or used by a University Peace Officer, a written Public Safety Incident Report and a Weapon Discharged/Use Report shall be prepared in accordance with The City University of New York Public Safety procedures. It shall be prepared and submitted to the Office of the University Public Safety Director with all relevant facts within 24 hours of the incident.

The ASP baton should be maintained in the same manner as all other public safety equipment. The baton should be kept dry. If exposed to water, salt air or perspiration, the baton should be opened and dried with a soft cloth. The butt cap, should be periodically checked to make sure it is tightly screwed onto the handle. The Tip should also be checked for looseness. If the Tip breaks loose, "Loc-Tite" or a similar product should be applied to the threads to secure it to the end section. The baton should be periodically checked for hairline fractures or excessive wear between sections. Fractures may occur if the baton is continually opened with too much force. Do not apply oil to the shaft section as this will affect the locking procedure of the baton.

inst.title: Rules and Regulations Regarding Firearms on Campus
b: This instruction codifies The City University of New York’s policy for the request and authorization of carrying firearms on campus.

It is the policy of The City University of New York that CUNY Peace Officers may bear firearms on campus only at the request of and authorization by the college presidents. In the case of the Central Office or Special Public Safety units which provide law enforcement services CUNY-wide, the request and authorization originates with the Chancellor or designee. Special Public Safety units shall carry firearms on a college campus only when specifically requested to and authorized by a CUNY college president.

Upon the request of a College President to arm CUNY Peace Officers at a particular campus, it shall be the responsibility of the University Director of Public Safety to determine the appropriate type of firearms to be used and to ensure that the designated CUNY Peace Officers receive the appropriate firearms training mandated by the New York State Department of Criminal Justice Services, Bureau of Municipal Police standards; the New York State Penal code; and the Criminal Procedure Law of The State of New York. The firearms training will be provided at no cost to the college, by a certified New York State Firearms Instructor selected by the Office of the University Director of Public Safety.

The University Director of Public Safety has been designated as the University Principal Owner and is the sole CUNY official authorized to purchase firearms on behalf of the University through the New York City Police Department for limited law enforcement purposes. CUNY firearms shall be purchased by the University Principal Owner through the NYPD designated gun custodian only upon request and authorization by the respective, college presidents or the Executive Vice Chancellor and Chief Operating Officer when the request pertains to the Central Office.
