IF POSSIBLE, OPEN ALL DOORS AND WINDOWS TO MINIMIZE THE PRIMARY DAMAGE CAUSED BY THE BLAST AND SECONDARY DAMAGE FROM FRAGMENTATION.
DO NOT ALLOW RE-ENTRY INTO THE BUILDING UNTIL THE BOMB HAS BEEN SAFELY REMOVED/DISARMED AND THE BUILDING DECLARED SAFE BY NYPD EMERGENCY SERVICES OR BOMB SQUAD.
ALL PERSONNEL SHOULD BE PLACED AT A PREDETERMINED SAFE LOCATION AWAY FROM SUSPECTED BOMB LOCATION.
ACTIONS TO BE TAKEN IF NO SUSPECTED OBJECT IS FOUND
The senior public safety/college official will confer with the police, if present, and be guided by their advice.
Having conferred with police personnel present and, if no clear or present danger exists, it is recommended that the building not be evacuated.
Notify the occupants of the condition and that their normal activities should continue.
The senior public safety official will prepare a detailed report of the incident and direct that public safety personnel resume their normal duties.

Restrictive Markings such as Confidential, • Visual Distractions (Fragile, Handle Personal, etc. With Care, etc.)

inst.title: Body Armor
b: This instruction prescribes The City University of New York policy for the use of Public Safety Department issued Body Armor as set forth by the University Director of Public Safety for the effective administration of campus public safety operations. These policies have been formulated within the scope and intent of the University Public Safety Initiative. Failure to comply with these policies, instructions and guidelines may result in a recommendation to appropriate college officials that disciplinary charges be filed.
The purpose of this policy is to provide officers of The City University of New York Public Safety Department with guidelines for the proper use and care of University issued body armor.

It is the policy of The City University of New York Public Safety Department to maximize the safety of its sworn public safety personnel through the use of body armor in compliance with established safety procedures. While body armor provides a significant level of protection, it is not a substitute for sound, basic safety procedures which should be employed. Not withstanding the disadvantages; including increased weight, greater discomfort and reduced mobility, the tremendous benefit to officer’s safety and well- being is obvious and prevails. This policy does not depict body armor as a freedom of choice issue, but rather as a mandated occupational safety equipment item. Body armor should be considered one of the most important pieces of defensive equipment.
All body armor issued must comply with current minimum protective standards as prescribed by the National Institute of Justice.
All sworn uniformed Peace Officers shall be issued body armor in accordance with University Public Safety Memorandum dated September 21, 1995, ref. Purchase of Soft Body Armor.
Body armor that is worn or damaged shall be replaced by the University Public Safety Office. Body armor that must be replaced due to misuse or abuse by the officer shall be paid for by the officer.
All CUNY Peace Officers assigned to patrol duties shall wear protective body armor at all times while on duty.

CUNY Peace Officers are required to wear the issued body armor while engaged in “field activities” (to include all activities in which officers are physically exposed to the public, regardless of whether their assignments normally involve direct enforcement) while on duty unless exempted as follows:
When a University-approved physician determines that an officer has a medical condition that would preclude use of body armor;
When the officer is involved in undercover or plainclothes work that his supervisor determines would be compromised by use of body armor;
When the College Public Safety Director determines that circumstances make it inappropriate to mandate body armor subject to approval by The University Director of Public Safety.
Officers shall wear only agency-approved body armor.
Supervisors shall be responsible for ensuring that body armor is worn and maintained as required by this policy through a periodic documented inspection of their subordinate’s body armor.
Periodic random testing of body armor shall be conducted by the individual responsible for the uniform supply function at the college through a certified laboratory.
There shall be an annual inspection by the Office of The University Director of Public Safety of all body armor for fit, cleanliness, signs of damage, abuse and wear.
Care and Maintenance of Body Armor

Although body armor is capable of stopping bullets, it is far from indestructible. Damage is not always readily visible and an officer could wear a damaged, ineffective vest with the mistaken impression that it is serviceable. This is why it is extremely important that vests are properly cleaned and cared for.

Body armor should be protected from sunlight or any other source of ultraviolet light because ultraviolet light breaks down the ballistic resistance of Kevlar. Officers should be taught that body armor should never be left in a vehicle exposed to sunlight and that outdoor drying of armor following cleaning is strictly prohibited. Just as with ultraviolet light, sunlight will destroy Kevlar’s ballistic capabilities. Damaged armor will have a slight color change and will appear to be more brown. More importantly, officers must be aware that damage can occur without visible detection.

Dry cleaning solvents, harsh detergents and bleach also damage Kevlar. Bleach is probably the most severe, even in very diluted amounts. Milder detergents of the home variety are safe but stronger detergents common to commercial laundering, as well as some dry cleaning solvents, can cause damage. It is strongly recommended that commercial laundering of body armor be avoided. Home washing should be performed by hand since tests have suggested that armor is damaged by machine washing, and possibly by machine drying as well.

Kevlar armor should be gently washed by hand with mild soap and water. Washing will not affect the water-repellency of the armor and full ballistic capability will return once the armor has dried. However, care should be taken to thoroughly rinse all soap residue from the armor because residue may accumulate over time and absorb enough water to impair ballistic efficiency. After the Kevlar armor is washed it should be gently hung indoors. Armor should never be hung on outside clotheslines, whether in the shade or on a cloudy day. Periodic inspection by the officer should be conducted after each washing for signs of damage or wear. The officer should look for fraying, cuts, stains, fading (indicating possible bleach damage) and “browning” (indicating possible ultraviolet light degradation).
Body armor should not be folded as ballistic resistance could become compromised at the point of the fold line.
Each officer is responsible for the proper storage of body armor in accordance with manufacture’s instructions and daily inspection for signs of damage and general cleanliness.
As dirt and perspiration may erode ballistic panels, each officer shall be responsible for cleaning his/her body armor in accordance with the manufacture’s instructions.
Officers are responsible for reporting any damage or wear to the ballistic panels or cover to the individual responsible for the uniform supply function.
The College Public Safety Training officer shall be responsible for maintaining the following information:
Technological advances in the body armor industry that may necessitate a change in body armor.
A description of weapons and ammunition currently in use, and whether or not issued body armor can withstand their impact.
Training programs that inform the officers about body armor, and emphasize its safe and proper use.

inst.title: Use of Handcuffs and Safeguarding of Prisoners
b: The City University of New York recognizes and respects the value and special integrity of each human life. Investing University Peace Officers with the lawful authority to use the necessary force to protect the public welfare, a careful balancing of all human interests is required. The ability to use force is the primary factor which distinguishes the law enforcement community form the remainder of the society it serves. No other segment of society is permitted this license. As a result of this responsibility, the use of force by public safety personnel comes under close scrutiny by both the public and the courts.

It is the policy of this University that its Peace Officers shall use only that force which is reasonably necessary to affect an arrest. The use of force on an individual who is already under control is deemed punishment and exceeds the bounds of all prevailing standards of law enforcement conduct and will not be tolerated. Officers authorized by law to use force may be held both criminally and civilly responsible for any inappropriate or excessive actions. No rule can be implemented which will include all occasions when a peace officer should handcuff a prisoner. Each incident must be handled according to the nature off the crime and the person who has committed it. It is the policy of the CUNY Public Safety Department to take the precautions necessary while handling and transporting prisoners, to protect the lives and safety of the officers, the public, and the person in custody. This instruction prescribes guidelines for (1) the use of handcuffs by members of the University Public Safety Department, (2) specifications for handcuffs and (3) safeguarding of prisoners while in the custody of sworn CUNY law enforcement officers (Peace Officers).

The use of force which may do harm to others must be exercised in a reasonable manner. In all instances, members of the service must conform with the laws governing the use of force (New York State Criminal Procedure Law). Persons authorized by law to use force are criminally and civilly responsible for any excessive use of that force. For the safety of the officer and the general public, handcuffs will be placed upon all prisoners who are charged with any offense and/or when a prisoner is being transported or escorted to any location. Handcuffs shall also be used when a prisoner is violent, and to prevent him from doing harm to himself or others. Additionally, in the case of an Emotionally Disturbed
Person (E.D.P.), handcuffs shall be used when there is a risk of injury to the E.D.P. or other person.
CUNY Peace Officers shall rear handcuff (double locked) all prisoners with their hands behind their back and palms facing outward.
The officer may handcuff the prisoner with his/her hands in front, or utilize other appropriate restraining devices where the prisoner:
is in an obvious state of pregnancy;
has injuries that could be aggravated by standard handcuffing procedures
Prisoners shall not be handcuffed to any part of the vehicle during transport and shall be secured in the vehicle by proper use of a seat belt.

Additional approved restraint devices (Flex-Cuffs) may be used to secure a prisoner who violently resists arrest or who manifests mental disorders such that he poses a threat to himself or to the public

Handcuffs shall be applied and adjusted to size before the frisk of a prisoner whenever possible. Handcuffing, at the early opportunity, is the best method of controlling a prisoner and they should be applied as soon as possible.

When transporting a prisoner from one location to another, the prisoner will always be handcuffed to prevent escape. In all instances where handcuffs are being utilized, they must be applied with the prisoner’s hands shackled behind him, where possible, the handcuffs may be applied through the prisoner’s belt. The arresting/transporting/escorting officer will never handcuff himself to a prisoner.

The prisoner will be thoroughly searched at the college of arrest prior to the transportation of the prisoner to a local precinct for booking, or to a facility of detention. Female prisoners will only be searched by another female. The
arresting officer must search the female’s coat, handbag or other belongings she may have in her possession and carefully OBSERVE her clothing and person for possible weapons.
If for any reason it is necessary to leave a prisoner unattended, he/she should be handcuffed to a solid, stationary object to prevent escape.
A member of the Public Safety Department shall treat a prisoner with only that level of restraint necessary to restore and/or maintain order, safety and security.
Prisoners should never be shackled to seats or other parts of moving automobiles, patrol, or other vehicles.
Officers shall make certain that handcuffs keys are properly secured.
Before applying the handcuffs, the key will be tested to assure that it will unlock the handcuffs.
The arresting officer will retain possession of the key until proper disposition of the prisoner has been made and the handcuffs removed.

Responsibility for the safeguarding of a prisoner in officer’s custody does not end when the officer reaches the precinct. Until the prisoner is searched, booked and lodged, he is still in the officer’s custody, and the fact that there is a delay in the booking procedure, necessitating a substantial wait, does not alleviate that responsibility.
Handcuffs shall be constructed of blue or nickel plated steel; weight to be at least 10oz.
They shall be double lock pin type which prevents opening with a pin and prevents a prisoner from further closing the cuffs thereby causing injury to his/her wrist.
Each cuff shall be separated by a swivel link.
Two keys shall be provided for each set of handcuffs.
Each set of handcuffs shall be equipped with a leather carrying case.
At the beginning and end of each tour of duty. All CUNY Public Safety vehicles regularly used for prisoner transport shall be inspected for readiness as follows:
all windows shall be intact, and outer door latches in proper working order;
rear seat door handles and window controls should be deactivated (locked); and
the interior shall be thoroughly searched to ensure that no weapons or contraband have been left or hidden within the vehicle.

Prior to placing a prisoner in the vehicle for transport, the transporting officer will again inspect the interior for weapons or contraband. The vehicle shall be searched again after the prisoner has been delivered to the appropriate NYPD precinct or other destination

Prisoners, whenever possible, should be transported in public safety vehicles. These vehicles are designed to provide maximum security against escape while the prisoner is in transit. However, the officer shall keep the prisoner under observation at all times while in transit, and the prisoner will always remain handcuffed.

If the prisoner is being transported to a hospital by ambulance, the officer shall ride in the body of the ambulance keeping always alert for the possibility of escape. The prisoner will always be restrained. The officer’s service firearm (where applicable) will be unloaded if the prisoner in mentally unbalanced.

In transporting prisoners by car, two officers should be in the car. If there is one prisoner, he should be seated in the rear on the right side with one officer in the rear seated behind the operator. If there are two or three prisoners, seat all in the rear with both officers in the front. The officer not driving the car shall face the rear and constantly observe the prisoners. The prisoner(s) will always be
handcuffed while in transit. If a “cage” type vehicle is being utilized to transport the prisoner(s), the prisoner(s) will be secured in the cage of the vehicle.
Any wheelchair, crutches, prosthetic devices, and medication should be transported with, but not in the possession of the prisoner.
Prisoners shall not be left unattended during transport. Any escape or attempt to escape shall be immediately reported to the communications center.

The following procedure will be adhered to in all instances where (1) a person is injured while being arrested, (2) a person being held in custody sustains injury, or (3) a person is arrested and is found to have injuries suffered prior to the time of arrest:

If the person is injured while being arrested or while in custody, supervising officer, Tour Commander or Director should immediately be informed of the incident and of the circumstances pertaining to the prisoner’s injury.
In any such instances of injury, the arresting officer (or the officer first learning of the injury, in case of injury while in custody) should arrange for immediate medical treatment.

All officers concerned shall prepare and submit a CUNY Public Safety Incident report to their College Public Safety Director with a copy to the University Director of Public Safety as to the complete circumstances of the incident. If the prisoner was injured by an officer as a result of the officer defending him/herself, this should be clearly indicated in the report and the prisoner(s) should be charged with assault in all instances where an officer is assaulted.
Signed statements should be obtained from witness other than the officers concerned.

Where a person arrested is found to have injures suffered prior to the arrest, the arresting officer should take necessary steps to substantiate that fact, including taking a signed statement from the arrested person detailing all the facts and conducting such further investigation as is necessary. Medical examination and attention should be promptly obtained as necessary.
When an arrest is effected and the prisoner requires hospitalization:
Transport the prisoner to the nearest hospital via ambulance or with the permission of the Tour Commander via public safety patrol vehicle.
Search prisoners in the presence of hospital personnel.
The escorting/guarding officer shall give the hospital authorities a receipt for the following:
Property dangerous to life or property.
Itemized list of personal property except clothing which is retained by the hospital
Record in his/her memorandum book all information necessary to process the arrest.
Not remove handcuffs from prisoner while in hospital unless requested by attending doctor.
If asked to leave treatment room for extraordinary medical reason by attending doctor:
handcuff prisoner if it does not prevent proper medical treatment.
request all escape routes be sealed or prisoner removed to a secured room or area.
stand immediately outside treatment room and maintain visual contact, if possible.
request attending physical to sign Memorandum Book.
Notify Tour Commander and request transportation to station house when prisoner is treated and released.
Notify Tour Commander if prisoner is admitted to the hospital.
The Tour Commander of the college of arrest shall:
Make necessary arrangements to have the escorting officer, if he is the arresting officer, relieved so he will be available to process the arrest.
Notify the N.Y.C.P.D. precinct in which the hospital of detention is located.
Notify the N.Y.C.P.D. precinct of arrest (if not aware of this arrest) of the circumstances of arrest and of the hospitalization of the prisoner.
Notify the N.Y.C.P.D. Court Division Unit (212) 347-5350 of the arrest and of the hospitalization of the prisoner.
If the prisoner id treated or hospitalized at other than a New York City Health and Hospital Corporation facility forward a report in a sealed envelope to:
N.Y.C. Health and Hospital Corporation Document Control Unit 125 Worth Street New York City 10013
Data and time of treatment or admission
Contact the administrator of the hospital and:
Determine how long the prisoner will be confined.

Request permission to take prisoner’s photograph and fingerprints and conduct BEDSIDE ARRAIGNMENT. If permission is denied due to prisoner’s physical condition, ascertain approximate date when prisoner can be arraigned. (About five (5) days are required to arrange for a BEDSIDE ARRAIGNMENT)

Determine if the prisoner is eligible for a Desk Appearance Ticket. If eligible have the proper document completed and served upon the prisoner. The guarding of the prisoner can be discontinued when he is served with the Desk Appearance Ticket.
If the prisoner is ineligible for a Desk Appearance Ticket, make arrangement for round-the-clock guard of the prisoner.
Notify parents or guardian of impending release of the prisoner if the prisoner is less than 18 years of age.
The officer guarding the prisoner shall:
Prevent unauthorized articled from being passed to prisoner.

Permit only the following persons, on official business, to interview prisoner: a. Ranking Officer of the CUNY Public Safety Department or N.Y.C.P.D. b. Detective c. D.A. or representative d. Clergyman e. Parole or probation officer f. Hospital personnel g. Social worker h. Lunacy commission appointee i. Federal law enforcement officer j. Ranking officer of other city agency or CUNY if prisoner is employee of said agencies
Recipient of notification from hospital superintendent with notification that prisoner is seriously ill.

Member of family after permission granted on official letterhead by station house supervisor – precinct of arrest or College Public Safety Director. Member of family include spouse, children 16 years or over, parents brothers and sister.
Enter in Memorandum Book, information concerning name, address and title of visitor.
Notify station house supervisor of precinct of arrest and college Tour Commander before end of tour of identity of all visitors.
Deliver transcript and rap sheet to relieving officer.
Notify College Public Safety Director when Fingerprints have been taken.
Ask prisoner if he wants Legal Aid and interpreter.
Inform the college Public Safety Director
Enter information concerning fingerprints, Legal Aide and interpreter on work sheet

The New York City department of Hospital Regulations state that a police/peace officer will unload his service firearm when entering a psychiatric ward. The officer will reload his service firearm after exiting the psychiatric ward.

Prisoner arraigned in court are usually not restrained, unless the judge orders otherwise. During the court appearance of the prisoner, the officer should be constantly observant of his prisoner and, if possible, station himself between the prisoner and the exit escape.

inst.title: Guidelines for Responding to Demonstrations
b: This instruction provides guidelines to the members of The City University of New York Public Safety Department responding to spontaneous demonstrations occurring on or near a campus.
The role of the Public Safety Department during these events is to:
Ensure the immediate safety of people and property within the affected area.
Gather information concerning the purpose of the demonstration and the identities of the leaders.
Relay the information to the appropriate college authorities in a timely manner.
If on campus, isolate and contain the demonstration pending the arrival of the appropriate college officials.
In an effort to accomplish the above objectives, College Public Safety Directors will ensure that local procedures and/or guidelines are clearly established or defined regarding the following:
Enforcement of college policies regarding demonstrations on campus.

Chain of command in assuming responsibility for reacting to demonstrations on campus including establishing a chain-of-command during joint operations involving University-level administrators or public safety personnel, and/or outside agencies.
Defining emergencies and the specific circumstances under which requests for outside assistance are to be made (e.g. S.A.F.E. Team, NYPD, FDNY, and EMS).

Maintaining a liaison with local police and other outside agencies to plan and coordinate responses to emergencies on campus to include designating an off campus mobilization/marshaling site for the agencies to rendezvous.
Maintaining current mobilization alert roster of all public safety personnel.
Designating alternate reporting sites during the "TAKEOVER" of key buildings or locations on campus, to avoid or minimize disruption of college functions.
Establishing arrest /transporting procedures for people taken into custody.
Defining the duties and responsibilities of public safety personnel during demonstrations to include:
First member of public safety on the scene.
Response and immediate assessment of situation.
Making all necessary assignments to safeguard people and property and maintaining control of key locations on campus (e.g. Public Safety Office, Administration Buildings).
Making notifications as required by local public safety policies.
Establishing a temporary headquarters at the scene with essential equipment and supplies, if necessary.
Controlling crowds and vehicular and pedestrian traffic.
Maintaining communications with college officials and other responding agencies.

The above guidelines are not intended to be construed as an all inclusive listing of factors that are to be considered when establishing local policies and procedures for responding to demonstrations on campus. These guidelines are to be used by the Directors of Public Safety as a basis for establishing an operations plan for demonstrations which conforms to the college rules and regulations that are presently in place at their respective campuses.

inst.title: General Policy – Use of Force
b: The City University of New York Public Safety Department is committed to preserving the value of life and the dignity of each individual. While performing their public safety and law enforcement duties, the most important responsibility of the CUNY Peace Officers is the preservation of life. Consistent with this principle, CUNY Peace Officers are directed to utilize only the minimum amount of force necessary to overcome resistance during enforcement actions. The City University of New York Public Safety Department has zero tolerance for the use of excessive force by any of its officers. As a matter of public safety policy, members of the service present during enforcement incidents are mandated to intervene where the use of force becomes excessive. Furthermore, members of the service with knowledge of excessive force being used by other law enforcement officers are required to immediately file an official report of the incident to their college supervisor. A copy of this report will be promptly forwarded to the Office of the University Director of Public Safety who will notify appropriate college officials and the Office of the Vice Chancellor for Legal Affairs. Failure to comply with these policies, instructions and guidelines may result in the filing of criminal charges and/or a recommendation to appropriate college officials that disciplinary charges be filed.
Regulations regarding the use of force:

Members of the service are prohibited from restraining an individual in a manner that restricts the flow of air or blood by compressing the windpipe or the carotid arteries on each side of the neck, or sitting, kneeling, or standing on the chest or back in a manner that compresses the diaphragm, in the course of effecting or attempting to effect an arrest. These tactics, which include trachea chokes, carotid restraints, commonly referred generically as “choke holds” are not authorized tactics by Division of Criminal Justice Services and the City University of New York Public Safety Department.

After an individual has been controlled and placed under custodial restraint using handcuffs or other authorized methods, the person should be positioned so as to promote free breathing. The subject should not be maintained in a face down position. The member of the service assuming custody of the subject should closely observe arrested/detained persons for any apparent injuries.
If a subject appears to be having difficulty breathing or otherwise demonstrates life threatening symptoms, medical assistance will be requested (via 911)
immediately. If appropriate, the supervisor present will direct that alternate means to maintain custody be utilized.
The use of restraints to “hog tie” subjects and the transportation of subjects in a face down position within any vehicle is prohibited.

inst.title: Random Drug Testing
b: With the exception of existing pre-employment and reasonable suspicion drug testing policies, this policy supersedes all existing drug policies related to CUNY Public Safety Department employees.

All members of The City University of New York Public Safety Department perform a sensitive and critical role in providing for the public safety of the campuses. In keeping with their law enforcement duties, they carry defensive equipment that could be dangerous or deadly if misused. The City University of New York is committed to the proper and efficient performance of that responsibility. Drug abuse on the part of members of the service destroys the proper and efficient performance of that responsibility by undermining the job performance of the abuser and potentially jeopardizing the safety of the college community.

In performing random drug testing, The City University of New York will follow the guidelines set forth in the Omnibus Transportation Employee Testing Act of 1991. Members of the City University of New York Public Safety Department will be subject to a random drug testing procedure to detect abuse. Pursuant to the Act, testing will be for the following drugs and their derivatives:
In addition, any drug/controlled substance determined to be illegal by the laws of the State of New York, will also be tested for.

CUNY will randomly test employees of the CUNY Public Safety Department; Directors, Lieutenants, Sergeants, Corporals, Patrol Officers, and Specialists actively serving with peace officer status. In an effort to establish a credible deterrent to illegal drug/controlled substance usage. The University’s goal is to ensure that members of the CUNY Public Safety Department do not use illegal drugs or abuse controlled substances and to maintain a high standard of performance in a drug free environment.

The University Director of Public Safety and/or his designee shall be responsible for the scheduling and administration of random drug tests. The selection of officers to be tested on a random basis shall be accomplished by placing the names of all members of the service in a computer program designed to produce random selection of 25% of the service. The actual selection procedure shall be performed by the University Director of Public Safety and/or his designee.

On the day when members of the Public Safety Department are to be randomly tested, a list of names and employee social security numbers will be generated at random until a sufficient number of officers are available to meet the established guidelines. The Office of the University Director of Public Safety will test at least 25% of all public safety department members in any calendar year utilizing this procedure.

The Office of University Public Safety will notify College Public Safety Directors and/or Managers by phone regarding scheduled drug tests for members of the service who have been randomly selected for drug testing. The College Public Safety Director and/or manager will make the proper entries in the “Drug Test Log” (see attached) and immediately notify the officer who is scheduled to be tested.
The following procedure will be followed:

Officers assigned to the day tour (0700 - 1530 hours, 0800 - 1630 hours, etc.) shall report to the designated testing lab site immediately upon notification (or as soon as the lab opens if that is later) unless there exists a defensible absence as listed in section IV of this operations order.

Randomly selected officers assigned to the afternoon tour (1400 - 2230, 1500 - 2330, etc.) shall report to the designated testing lab site at 1400 hours on the following day unless there exists a defensible absence as listed in section IV of this operations order (also refer to paragraph VI - overtime).

Officers assigned to the midnight tour (2230 - 0700 hours, 2300 - 0730 hours, etc.) shall report to the designated testing site lab immediately following their tour of duty unless there exists a defensible absence excuse as listed in section IV of this operations order (also refer to paragraph VI - overtime).
Partners in Safety 408 West 45th Street -- (between 9th/10th Avenues) New York, NY 10036 Monday - Friday 0830 – 1630 hours - Telephone: (212) 727-8637

The random selection of a member of the CUNY Public Safety Department will not result in that member’s name being removed from the list. Thus, due to the random nature of the selection process, officers may be tested more than once in a given year.
The drug testing will be conducted by analyzing an employee’s urine sample. The officer will be required to provide a urine sample at the designated laboratory; currently Partners in Safety.

The lab technician (collector) will seal and label the urine sample, complete a chain of custody form and prepare the sample and all accompanying documentation for shipment to a drug-testing laboratory. The analysis will be performed by a certified laboratory monitored by the U. S. Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS). The sample will remain sealed and stored at the laboratory. If the test proves inconclusive, the officer will be directed to be tested again within 30 days. If the sample is confirmed positive for the presence of illegal drugs/controlled substances, the officer will have 72 hours from the time he is notified by the University Director of Public Safety and or his/her designee to appeal, which may include a request to re-test the same sample at another DHHS certified laboratory for analysis at the officer’s expense.
If the results are still positive, for any of the screened drugs, a confirmation test will be performed using gas chromatography/mass spectrometry (GCMS) analysis.

If there still is a positive result, the employee will be interviewed by the designated City University of New York Medical Review Officer to verify whether the positive drug test resulted from unauthorized use of illegal drugs/controlled substances.
When the designated Medical Review Officer determines that the positive test result is from the unauthorized use of an illegal drug/controlled substances, the following will occur:
The designated Medical Review Officer will notify the University Director of Public Safety or designee, of the test result.
Upon notice of a confirmed positive drug test, the University Personnel Director will be notified by the University Director of Public Safety. The University

Personnel Director will then notify the employee’s college. The officer will be immediately relieved of duty and subject to disciplinary charges with a recommendation for dismissal from the service in accordance with the applicable collective bargaining agreement. Probationary/provisional officers not entitled to disciplinary hearings under the collective bargaining agreement will be referred to the College Director of Personnel for immediate dismissal from the service.

Members of the Public Safety Department selected for random drug testing pursuant to this procedure must appear for the scheduled submission unless they are absent from duty on the day of notification due to:
Documented Bereavement (in accordance with Blue Collar Contract and/or any applicable University personnel policies and guidelines.)
Transportation Failure (as defined in the Blue Collar Contract Article IX Section 13)

Members of the service must provide written documentation (within 30 days) to the Office of the University Director of Public Safety regarding the aforementioned absences if their names appear on the randomly generated list.

Failure to appear due to any of the above defensible absences will require a re-scheduled drug/controlled substance test, within 45 days of return to duty on a date to be determined by the University Director of Public Safety.

Members of the Public Safety Department MUST report for testing as scheduled and if assigned to the day tour (7x3, 8x4, etc.,) within three (3) hours of notification during lab hours of operation. Failure to report or failure to comply with laboratory instructions will be deemed sufficient reason under the Reasonable Drug Suspicion Policy for officers to be tested. This policy will then take precedence over the Random Drug Testing Policy Operations Instruction. In addition, officers refusing to be tested will be subject to disciplinary charges with a recommendation for dismissal from the CUNY Public Safety Department.

At the test site, officers will be required to prepare all forms associated with the testing process. Officers scheduled to be tested will present their New York State driver’s license and test authorization form to insure that the correct individual has reported for testing. Failure to adhere or comply with any of the above instructions will be deemed a “Refusal to Cooperate” and as such, the employee will be subject to disciplinary charges.

Members of the service working the afternoon tour (1400-2230, 1500-2330, etc.) or midnight tour (2230-0700 hours, 2300-0730 hours, etc.) will be reporting to the designated laboratory on an overtime basis. This overtime expense (not to exceed 4 hours) will be borne by the individual officer’s college of assignment.
All drug testing results and related information will be maintained by the Office of University Public Safety Director and will be designated as HIGHLY CONFIDENTIAL.

Any employee of the Public Safety Department covered by this policy, who prior to selection for testing wishes to make a voluntary disclosure concerning drug related behavior may do so only to the College Personnel Director in accordance with University Personnel Policy Memorandum dated September 29, 1998. Voluntary admissions to public safety supervisory personnel will subject the officer to the University Reasonable Suspicion Policy (Operations Instruction #8).

behavior may do so only to the College Personnel Director in accordance with University Personnel Policy Memorandum dated September 29, 1998. Voluntary admissions to public safety supervisory personnel will subject the officer to the University Reasonable Suspicion Policy (Operations Instruction #8).

inst.title: Arrests – General
b: This CUNYDPS Operation Instruction is provided as a guideline to assist University Peace Officers with the processing of arrested persons.

It is the policy of The City University of New York that University Peace Officers will impartially perform their law enforcement duties, exercising necessary discretion, to ensure a safe and secure environment for the University Community.
Members of the CUNY Public Safety Department who exercise their arrest authority in performance of their duties will follow the following procedure:
After an arrest has been effected and the prisoner has been handcuffed, an immediate field search/frisk of prisoner must be conducted in accordance with Operations Instruction #7.
Prior to questioning, the arresting officer must advise the prisoner of his/her Miranda rights, unless the prisoner is a juvenile.

If the prisoner is a juvenile (less than 16 years of age), notification to the parent or guardian should be made immediately, as they must be present when Miranda rights are read. The juvenile can be questioned if he/she waives such rights in the presence of the parent or guardian. If the parent or guardian objects to the questioning or requests an attorney for the juvenile, the questioning must stop immediately, even if the juvenile is willing to answer questions.

Miranda rights need to be given in a language that the prisoner understands. If the prisoner request an attorney, all questioning must stop until the attorney is present and waives the prisoner’s right to remain silent.
Members of the service will (in lieu of immediate transport to an NYPD facility), transport the prisoner to the College Public Safety Office for further processing.

NOTE: In arrest situations, Members of the Service must exercise caution when transporting prisoners. If the arresting officer determines that circumstances warrant the assistance of the NYPD, they should request (via 911/Division Radio) transport to an NYPD facility equipped to house prisoners (local precinct or central booking – as appropriate).
Arrival at the College Public Safety Office

Upon arrival at the Campus Public Safety Office, the arresting officer will present the prisoner to the ranking college public safety supervisor and articulate the charges and circumstances of the arrest.

The supervisor will review the circumstances surrounding the arrest and determine if the prisoner can be detained for processing at the campus (summons) or transported to the appropriate NYPD facility for further processing.
Arresting officer will conduct the following checks via the eJusticeNY Integrated Justice Portal:
Wanted Persons Missing Persons Parole File
Colleges that are not equipped with eJusticeNY may request assistance from University Public Safety (646) 664-2907.
Will review information provided by eJusticeNY and determine eligibility for summons processing. Determination of eligibility will be based on verification of the following:

Supervisors must ensure proper identification of the suspect prior to authorizing processing for a summons. Any suspect that cannot be properly identified to the satisfaction of the supervisor on duty should be transported to the appropriate NYPD facility for further investigation and/or processing. A verified eJusticeNY “HIT” requires processing through an NYPD facility.
If the prisoner is determined to be eligible for a summons, the arresting officer will prepare the appropriate summons in accordance with CUNYDPS Operation Instruction Number 29.
Upon the arrival to the NYPD facility the arresting officer must:
Conduct a thorough search of the prisoner in the presence of the desk officer;
Lodge prisoner in holding cell, unless otherwise instructed by the desk officer;
Update NYPD facility logs as necessary;
Prepare an Online Booking Arrest Worksheet and any additional forms consistent with the arrest and submit to the desk officer for approval;
Log into the Omniform system and complete the Online Booking and obtain the arrest number generated by the system;
Have the prisoner finger and palm printed utilizing the Livescan system. In addition, digital photos of the prisoner must be taken to generate a Prisoner Movement Slip;
Voucher and secure any evidence, if applicable;
Have desk officer review all documents for thoroughness and accuracy;
Upon completion of the process at the NYPD facility, inform the desk officer that the prisoner will be removed and transported to Central Booking.
NOTE: Arresting/Escorting officer must have copies of the Prisoner Movement Slip with photo and the Online Booking System Arrest Worksheet with arrest number and check digit indicated.
Upon arrival to Central Booking, the arresting officer must:
Present all documents related to the arrest to the desk officer;
Have the prisoner evaluated by FDNY Emergency Medical Services personnel on-site;

The arresting officer must report to the District Attorney’s Office to draw up a court complaint of all verbal and written statements made by the defendant, and any procedures used to assist a witness or complainant to identify the defendant.
The arresting officer will prepare the CUNYDPS Incident Report and provide copies of all documents related to the arrest.

The supervisor assigned will ensure that the above procedure is completed accurately and that all documents related to the arrest including the eJusticeNY printouts are forwarded to campus CUNYDPS management for review and processing.
CUNYDPS Operations Instruction Number 7 – Search of Arrested Persons
CUNYDPS Operations Instruction Number 29 - Criminal Court Summons Processing

inst.title: Criminal Court Summons Processing
b: This CUNYDPS Operations Instruction is provided as a guideline to assist City University of New York (CUNY) Peace Officers with the process of obtaining and processing New York State (NYS) / New York City Summons Forms. The steps outlined in this instruction ensure compliance with the Criminal Court City of New York – NYC Criminal Court Automated Summons Processing System Memorandum (2/24/00).

It is the policy of The City University of New York that University Peace Officers will impartially perform their law enforcement duties, exercising necessary discretion, to ensure a safe and secure environment for the University Community. University Peace Officers will obtain and issue summonses in accordance with this policy and established college summons form distribution guidelines.
Members of the Public Safety Department will obtain and process summons forms as indicated below:
NYS Criminal Court Summons (“C” summons) forms will be obtained by each college from the University Office of Public Safety.
University Office of Public Safety 555 West 57th Street, Suite 1030 New York, NY 10019
Forms will then be returned to the command college and secured for later distribution in accordance with established college policy.
Accounting and Distribution at Command College
Summons Forms must be stored in a secure space and accounted for at all times. The College Director of Public Safety (or designee) will issue summons forms as needed to any duly sworn Peace Officer.

Once supplied with a sealed package of summonses, the University Peace Officer will (in the presence of the issuing supervisor), open the package and verify the contents. The officer will then record the issued summons forms by number on the supplied Summons Control Card. As each summons is issued, the officer will record the date and pedigree information as required on the card for each summons issued. Once all twenty issued summons forms are used, the Summons Control Card will be returned to the designated supervisor for storage.

NOTE: In lieu of the above, campuses may issue individual forms for each offense as needed and store the remaining forms in a secure location. Supervisors would then be responsible for verification of the sealed package contents

Once it has been determined that a summons will be issued, such form shall be prepared by The University Peace Officer as prescribed in Operation Instruction #28, Arrests - General. Once completed, the form will be submitted to the designated supervisor for further processing.

The designated supervisor will then review the completed summons and ensure compliance with Criminal Procedure and Penal Law. The supervisor (or designated administrative officer) will then separate the form(s) for distribution as follows:
White Copy: Original – Forward to Central Receiving Unit (see below)
Pink Copy: Provided to defendant for appearance in Criminal Court (Penal Law Violations, NYC Administrative Code)
Yellow Copy: Retain along with related agency records
Green Copy: Retain along with related agency records
Buff Card Stock: Retained by the issuing Peace Officer
All summons forms regardless of the borough where it was served must be forwarded within Five (5) business days to:
Chief Clerk’s Office 1 Centre Street, Suite 1629 New York, NY 10007
Summons Issued in Error or Voided
Summons Forms may be voided by the College Director of Public Safety or designee.
Summons Forms not forwarded to the Chief Clerk’s Office may be voided as follows:
Prepare a CUNYDPS Incident Report indicating the reason(s) for voiding the summons.
Attach all copies of the summons forms to the report
File report in accordance with established individual college policy
Notify the defendant that they do not need to appear in court
Summons Forms already forwarded to the Chief Clerk’s Office may be voided as follows:

The College Director of Public Safety must write a letter addressed to the Senior Court Clerk – Citywide Summons Operations indicating the need to void the summons and the specific reasons why it should be voided.
The completed letter must then be forwarded to the following address:
Office of the Senior Court Clerk Citywide Summons Operations 1 Centre Street, Suite 1629 New York, NY 10007
The College Director of Public Safety (or designee) will then prepare the following forms:
Prepare a CUNYDPS Incident Report indicating the reason(s) for voiding the summons
Attach all copies of the summons forms and letter to the report
File report in accordance with established individual college policy
Defendant will be notified by the court not to appear
Each campus is required to maintain a summons control log. Upon issuing a summons, the officer must record the following information:
Arresting Officer’s Name, Rank, Shield, and Tax ID Number
NOTE: If a summons is issued in error or voided an annotation must be made to the summons control log.
Criminal Court of New York City, Administrative Memorandum 2/24/00

inst.title: CUNY Peace Officer Designation Procedure
b: Pursuant to New York State Criminal Procedure Law Section 2.10 subsection 79, the Board of Trustees of The City University of New York is authorized to appoint members of The City University of New York (CUNY) Department of Public Safety as Peace Officers. As such, the Board of Trustees has authorized the Chancellor to administer the Peace Officer designation in accordance with this procedure.

Upon appointment to a covered CUNY Public Safety Department Civil Service Title where Peace Officer status is authorized, the Director of Public Safety (or designee) at the employing college shall ensure that the Peace Officer candidate submits an original CUNY Application for Peace Officer Deputization Form to the Office of the University Director of Public Safety. Upon successful completion of the required background investigation and training programs, the University Director of Public Safety (or designee) shall recommend to the Chancellor or designee to deputize such officers as Peace Officers.

Pursuant to action of the Board of Trustees, the Chancellor and his/her designees are authorized to withhold Peace Officer status until all training and background checks have been completed in a satisfactory manner. This means that Peace Officer status will only commence upon the Officer being sworn in by a designee of the Chancellor. The Board also has empowered the Chancellor’s designee to suspend or revoke Peace Officer status at any time under appropriate circumstances.

Eligibility In order to be eligible for appointment as a CUNY Peace Officer, the candidate must be of good character, as more specifically defined in these rules, cooperate in a background investigation by the Office of the University Director of Public Safety, and possess the following qualifications:
Be a citizen of the United States and resident of New York State.

Have no record of convictions for any felony or serious offense as enumerated in § 265.00 (17) of the New York State Penal Law. If an applicant presents a Certificate of Relief from Disabilities for a conviction as aforesaid, consideration shall be given to the circumstances of the underlying arrest, the age of the applicant when arrested, the time elapsed
since the occurrence of the act which led to the arrest and conviction, and the subsequent conduct of the applicant.
Be at least 21 years of age at the time of appointment.
If discharged from the military service, have an honorable discharge.
Be able to perform the essential functions of a Peace Officer with or without reasonable accommodations.

In addition to lacking any of the above qualifications, candidates for CUNY Peace Officer designation may be also disapproved by failure to meet character requirements as disclosed by a background investigation. This determination shall be based upon a review of the circumstances of previous arrests, employment records, reports of misconduct reflecting on character or any other pertinent records or information.

All applicants shall be fingerprinted upon the filing of the application on forms provided by the Office of the University Director of Public Safety. A processing fee as required by the New York State Division of Criminal Justice Services (DCJS) shall be paid by the applicant officer (money order made payable to The City University of New York in the amount of $75.00). The Office of the University Director of Public Safety will maintain an escrow account with DCJS for processing fingerprints.
Upon notification by the Office of the University Director of Public Safety, the following items shall be provided by the candidates:
Two color photos 1½ x 1½ inches, front view, taken within the past thirty (30) days.
Certified copy DD214 and military discharge; if any.
Proof of NYS residence (telephone bill, lease or notarized letter of verification).
Handgun license or rifle/shotgun permit, if applicable.
New York State Department of Motor Vehicles Drivers License.

During the investigation process, the candidate must immediately notify the Office of the University Director of Public Safety of any correction or modification of the information provided in the original application, or any change in his or her status, which may be relevant to the processing of the application.
CUNY Peace Officers and the Director of Public Safety at the college of assignment (or designee) shall immediately notify the Office of the University Director whenever such CUNY Peace Officer is:

● Arrested. ● Suspended from employment. ● Terminated from employment. ● Unable to perform the duties of a Peace Officer due to a medical condition or for some other reason. ● Transferred to a position not requiring appointment as a peace officer. ● Involved in an incident which demonstrates conduct which is contrary to the purpose of appointment as a CUNY Peace Officer, i.e., the protection of property, or the safety of specific individuals or the public at large, and to her/his continued designation as a CUNY Peace Officer (pursuant to established Personnel and Public Safety policy).

Upon receipt of this notification from the CUNY Peace Officer, Director of Public Safety (or designee) at college of assignment, or otherwise, the Office of the University Director of Public Safety shall then issue an Initial Investigation Report.

This report will serve to notify the CUNY Peace Officer and the Director of Public Safety (or designee) at the college of assignment that the officer’s Peace Officer status is under review (continued until investigation is complete), suspended or revoked.

Peace Officer status may also be suspended or revoked by the University Director of Public Safety (or designee) on his/her own initiative for any of the reasons enumerated above, or upon a finding that a condition exists which would be cause for a disapproval of an application.

The cancellation, suspension or revocation of Peace Officer status shall be in addition to (not in lieu of) disciplinary action in accordance with established University policy. Once notification has been made that Peace Officer status has been cancelled, suspended or revoked, the CUNY Peace Officer must immediately deliver his/her University issued Peace Officer Shield and Identification card without delay to the Office of the University Director of Public Safety no later than the next business day. Upon surrender, the officer will be provided with a receipt that will serve as proof of return and a copy thereof will be forwarded to the college of assignment.
Appeal from Written Notice of Determination of Revocation

All appeals concerning revocation of Peace Officer status shall be made to the University Director of Public Safety. Upon receiving a Notice of Revocation, members of the service may present any documents, reports or statements to the University director of Public Safety (or designee) for consideration within 10 days of receipt of the revocation notice. Within 30 days of the date of the receipt of an appeal, the University Director of Public safety (or designee) will inform the appealing member of the service of his/her final determination. If the determination is to deny the appeal, the member has the right to further appeal in an Article 78 Proceeding in Civil Court.
In addition to the established Code of Conduct guidelines as outlined in CUNY Public Safety Instruction #1, CUNY Peace Officers are advised that:
It is a crime for a CUNY Peace Officer to represent himself/herself as a Police Officer (§ 190.25 of the New York State Penal Law).

CUNY Peace Officers are to comply with Operations Instruction # 29 - Administrative Processing of Summonses for arrests where a summons is appropriate. In all other cases, CUNY Peace Officers must process arrested persons in accordance with Operations Instruction # 28, Processing of Arrested Persons, and, as necessary, transport the prisoner without delay to the appropriate NYPD facility (local precinct or central booking).
CUNY Peace Officers shall promptly notify the Office of the University Director of Public Safety and the Director of Public Safety at the college
of assignment of any change in residence, telephone number or employment status.

In accordance with established University policy, if a CUNY Peace Officer is arrested or issued a summons for any reason (other than minor traffic violations), he/she must immediately notify the Director of Public Safety at the college of assignment and the Office of the University Director of Public Safety.

Persons appointed as CUNY Peace Officers are mandated to receive and successfully complete training pursuant to New York State Criminal Procedure Law § 2.30 (1), within 12 months of their designation. Such training will be provided by the Office of the University Director of Public Safety in a manner consistent with City University Public Safety Department established training curriculum and New York State Division of Criminal Justice Service Guidelines. Officer must also attend a minimum number of hours of In-Service training as prescribed by the New York State Division of Criminal Justice Services and the Office of the University Director of Public Safety.

inst.title: Active Shooter Incident Response Protocol
b: The City University of New York recognizes the potential danger of an Active Shooter Incident to the University Community. College Public Safety Departments will rely on a response from the NYPD in Active Shooter Incidents. Accordingly, the below listed policy has been formulated in order to maximize an effective Public Safety response to these possible incidents.

Whenever a College Public Safety Department receives notification of an incident in progress where an Active shooting Incident is taking place, the following procedures should be followed in accordance with established Incident Command System (ICS) Protocols.
Upon receiving notification of an active shooting incident in progress, the dispatcher will:
Obtain as many details as possible
Notify the Senior Public Safety Official on duty
Upon direction by the Senior Public Safety Department Official on duty, dispatch Public Safety Officers to the general vicinity
Notify college Administration Officials in accordance with Emergency Management Plan
Notify University Public Safety in accordance with Operation Instruction #13 – Public Safety Notification
First Public Safety Officer on Scene

The first Public Safety Officer responding to the incident will respond only to the general vicinity of the incident and will take proper cover. Their responsibility is to safely observe in order to keep their dispatcher apprised of the situation by providing the following information; and to attempt to establish an initial secure perimeter.
The exact location and type of incident.
The time of the incident i.e. ongoing, past, etc.
The type and number of weapons involved, if known.
The number and description of participants involved.
Known injuries and the need for any medical assistance.

Prior to the arrival of the NYPD, armed CUNY Public Safety Officer(s) may, given the totality of the circumstances known to them during an active shooter incident, engage the active shooter for the sole purpose of protecting lives.
First Public Safety Supervisor on the Scene
The first Public Safety Supervisor on the Scene will take command of the incident
Establish communication with the New York City Police Department to provide additional information.
Locate the nearest safe location and establish a secure perimeter. Prevent others from entering the area and provide a clear path for others to evacuate.
Facilitate NYPD response by designating officers to direct NYPD responders to the scene.

Upon the arrival of the first NYPD personnel, the designated Public Safety Officer in charge will relay all necessary information and turn over Incident Management, to the NYPD. NYPD will then direct all law enforcement activities for the remainder of the incident.

CUNY Public Safety Personnel will coordinate with NYPD to assist in any evacuation or lock-down of buildings and surrounding area. They should also be prepared to provide information on Floor Plans, HVAC, Hazmat materials, Phone and Building Security Systems
At the direction of the NYPD will coordinate with FDNY for medical treatment and establishing triage and assembly areas.
Request activation of the College Emergency Response and Recovery Plan at the appropriate level
Assist in coordination of College Contingency Planning

inst.title: Use of Department Vehicles
b: The purpose of this policy is to ensure proper and safe usage, maintenance, serviceability and cleanliness of Department vehicles.

Department vehicles shall be used with the utmost care, only in furtherance of official business, and in complete compliance with the policies and directives of both the College and University Departments of Public Safety and the laws of the City and State of New York.

Officers shall exercise judgment and care with due regard for life and property when responding to campus calls for service. Officers shall stop, or be able to stop, for all traffic control devices and/or potential obstacles. Data and research clearly show that the most dangerous location for a responding vehicle is at an intersection. Officers shall come to a complete stop at all intersections in which the right of way is not clearly evident by a green traffic signal or the lack of a stop sign.

Operation of Department vehicles shall be in accordance with the Vehicle and Traffic Laws of the State of New York and Department guidelines. Officers are cautioned that negligence in the operation of Department vehicles will result in disciplinary action, and may result in criminal or civil sanctions.

MOTOR VEHICLE PURSUITS ARE STRICTLY PROHIBITED UNDER ANY CIRCUMSTANCES. If it is determined that an immediate apprehension of a suspect(s) is necessary, all relevant details regarding exact location, direction of travel and type of incident, times, description of participants, vehicles and weapons involved etc. will be transmitted to NYPD for their action.

Officers are authorized to respond with emergency lights and sirens on campus only under the most exigent of circumstances, such as to provide warning regarding a dangerous situation or in response to a life or death emergency. If the vehicle operator deems it such an emergency, a radio call to dispatch or to a
supervisor, stating the nature of the emergency, must be made and an emergency response via 911 must be summoned as well.
By law, CUNY Public Safety vehicles are not authorized to operate emergency lights and sirens outside of CUNY property.
Department vehicles shall not be driven in such a manner as to constitute reckless disregard for the safety of persons or property.
Use of patrol vehicles for routine/non-emergency traffic stops is prohibited.

Civilians shall be transported in Department vehicles only when necessary to accomplish a Public Safety function. Such transportation shall be done in accordance with departmental policy or at the direction of a supervisory officer. The transport of aided or injured individuals is prohibited.
To assure the safety of all personnel, safety belts shall be worn by drivers and passengers in all Department vehicles and/or any vehicles used for Department purposes.

Officers observing the necessity for maintenance or repairs shall report this fact to their immediate supervisor and complete a department Vehicle Inspection Report. If an officer feels that an assigned vehicle is unsafe for operation, a supervisory officer shall be consulted, a determination made and said vehicle either removed from or returned to service.
Officers shall not push or tow disabled vehicles with their assigned departmental vehicles, unless so authorized by a supervisor.
Except in an emergency, Department vehicles will not be operated on unpaved roads or over terrain, or in any manner which may be expected to damage the vehicle.
It shall be the responsibility of the operator of any Department vehicle to which he/she is assigned, to inspect said vehicle at the beginning and conclusion of each
mobile assignment. Each operator will make certain that the vehicle is adequately fueled during the tour and will discard any trash and ensure that the vehicle is reasonably clean.
(Upon receipt of an assigned vehicle, any cleanliness violations from prior operator should be documented and reported to a supervisor).

Operators shall report any damage to their supervisor prior to the vehicle’s operation. They shall also inspect Department authorized equipment contained in the vehicle to insure its presence and serviceability, reporting any deficiency to a supervisor. All officers shall also conduct a thorough search of said vehicle for contraband which may have been secreted within the vehicle prior to their operation of that vehicle.
Smoking is prohibited in all Department vehicles.
All vehicle operators will complete a department Vehicle Inspection Report upon completion of all vehicle operation assignments.

To ensure that Department vehicles, assigned equipment and related records are being properly maintained, each Sunday, after the day tour is posted (or at other times as directed by the Director or Assistant Director) a designated supervisor will inspect each Department vehicle for:
Current and valid New York State inspection and registration stickers
Supervisor will then complete and submit a department Vehicle Inspection Report documenting his findings.

All marked Department vehicles shall bear the CUNY Public Safety logo and the words “Public Safety”. The words “Campus Police” will no longer be acceptable on a Department of Public Safety marked vehicle.

inst.title: Special Assistance for Events [SAFE] Team
b: The City University of New York has established a Special Assistance for Events [SAFE] Team. This team, comprised of Public Safety Officers from multiple campuses and the Central Office, receive specialized training in crowd control, dignitary protection and addressing other issues that arise at large events or special functions, such as concerts, celebrations, demonstrations or meetings. The Team responds to emergency situations as well as assists campuses in advance of and at scheduled events.

The purpose of this instruction is to establish requirements and procedures for membership on the SAFE Team as well as to describe the circumstances when the SAFE team should be deployed authority for deploying the Team and operations of the team.
Deployment of SAFE Team The SAFE Team is directed to respond upon authorization of a College President or designee or for Central Office locations, the Chief Operating Officer or designee.

Planned Events Operations that do not require an immediate response may be delegated to SAFE Team Leaders. Under the direction from the Deputy University Director of Public Safety, Team Leaders have the responsibility for determining the scope of the detail, planning, managing, and the assignment of personnel.

Unplanned Events Operations that require immediate response and rapid deployment are delegated to the highest ranking Public Safety Official on scene until relieved by a higher Public Safety Official, or University Public Safety designee, including but not limited to a SAFE Team Leaders.

Chain of Command All members of the SAFE Team are equal regardless of rank and report to a University Public Safety Official or a Team Leader at an event; however there may be times where a member will be assigned to supervise a group of other members; this assignment will be directed by a University Public Safety Official, SAFE Team Leader or designee.

Criteria for Selection to the Special Assistance for Events [SAFE] Team Members of Service will be carefully screened and selected, taking into consideration his/her experience as a peace officer, verbal skills, problem solving skills, and responsibility. The following is the minimum criteria to be utilized by the Department in the selection process of a potential SAFE Team member.
Two (2) years of service as a Peace Officer with the Public Safety Department
Letter of recommendation from College Public Safety Director
Exhibit a high level of physical condition and agility.
Demonstrate satisfactory levels of performance on all evaluations within the past 18 months.

Upon completion of interviews process the Team Leaders will make their recommendations in writing to the University Deputy Director of Public Safety, by listing all of the candidates interviewed in order of preference along with their justification for the recommendations.
Membership Once selected, members must complete a six (6) month probationary period and remain in good standing, including:
Maintaining a good attendance and punctuality record on campus as well as at SAFE Team events
Abide by the University Operations Guide with regards to uniforms and appearance
Maintain good disciplinary standing on assigned campus

SAFE Team Training The SAFE team is trained in, although not limited to respond to Crowd Control, Civil Disorder, Dignitary Protection, Mass Arrest Procedures, Protests and Demonstrations. Members of service who serve as SAFE Team members will receive training two (2) times a year, January and August (these times may vary depending on University operations and or emergencies that may arise). Members of the SAFE team may be required to attend the firearms long course as regulated by the Department of Criminal Justice Services (DCJS). Members who complete the firearms long course will possess and maintain a NYPD pistol permit; and are required to attend a mandated annual requalification course required by DCJS.

Issued Equipment The department will provide members of the SAFE Team with specialized equipment for protection and to facilitate the successful resolution of tactical operations. This equipment is the property of the University and it is the responsibility of the officer to maintain and safeguard this equipment. The officer must sign a receipt acknowledging possession of the equipment; and upon separation from the SAFE Team all equipment must be returned to the University Office of Public Safety. Only equipment authorized by the University Office of Public Safety shall be used.
- Radio (issued at detail) - Riot Helmet w/shield and grill - Straight Baton - Tactical Gloves - Flex Cuffs - Equipment Bag
All departmental equipment must be brought all SAFE Team details and is subject to inspection.

Uniforms Uniform assignment for all SAFE Team details is the uniform of the day as per operation instruction # 6 unless, otherwise directed by the University Office of Public Safety. The following uniform items are prohibited from being worn during any SAFE Team detail.
- Bicycle Uniform (Polo Shirts/Pants/Shorts) - Baseball Caps - Sneakers - Ski Caps

Separation SAFE Team membership will be considered an at will relationship between the officer, his/her college Director of Public Safety, and the University Office of Public Safety. Thus SAFE Team membership may be terminated by the member for any reason and without penalty. In addition, this membership may be terminated by the college Director of Public Safety and the University Office of Public Safety for any justifiable reason.

inst.title: Bicycle Patrol Unit
b: The Department of Public Safety is committed to providing a safe and secure environment for the University Community. This Operation Instruction is to establish policy governing the use and purpose of the Uniform Bicycle Patrol Unit.

The Department of Public Safety has implemented the use of bicycles by officers whenever such methods will result in an improved level of service to the University Community. Department owned patrol bicycles shall be operated in accordance with all applicable New York State/City laws, and bicycle patrol guidelines. Patrol bicycles are to be operated with due regard for the safety of the officer and the public. This policy is applicable to all officers assigned to the Bicycle Patrol Unit.

The Department of Public Safety Bicycle Patrol Training course covers basic cycling principles and skills; including riding in traffic, bike fit, gearing and cadence, health and fitness, basic maintenance, emergency handing skills, hazard evasion, night riding, patrol tactics, legal issues, traffic law, and scenarios. To successfully complete the course Members of Service must pass a written examination, an on-bike road skills test, and an on-bike police cycling skills test.
Members of Service that have successfully completed the Bicycle Patrol training course must adhere to the following procedures.
Members of Service not assigned to the Bicycle Patrol Unit shall not operate a bicycle prior to completing an approved training program.
Approved helmets shall be worn at all times when the bicycle is in operation.
If patrol bicycle is left unattended in a public place, it shall be secured unless an emergency prevents it. In that case, the bicycle should be secured as soon as possible.
A written notification, in the form of an incident report of any damage to a patrol bicycle must be submitted to a supervisor immediately.
When officers ride at night, a headlamp and rear light shall be used in accordance with law.

The bicycle uniform is a special duty uniform that shall be worn in accordance with CUNYDPS Operation Instruction number 6.21, 6.22. This uniform will only be worn if assigned to bicycle patrol unless given prior approval by the Director of Public Safety. Bicycle Officers shall have the regular uniform of the day readily available in case reassignment is necessary.
Ballistic vest shall be worn at all times in accordance with Operation Instruction 23.
The Director of Public Safety shall have the discretionary authority to allow the wearing of other approved uniform and equipment items as necessary to meet operational needs.

Members of Service operating a patrol bicycle are responsible for the daily maintenance of the bicycle and shall conduct a pre-tour and post-tour inspection. Deficiencies shall be reported to the bicycle patrol supervisor.
The bicycle patrol supervisor is responsible for maintaining the bicycle equipment beyond the daily maintenance level. These duties include, but are not limited to:

Repair equipment within the means provided by the College. Make recommendations to his/her immediate supervisor for sending equipment out for repair. Patrol bicycle requiring maintenance and/or repairs beyond the capability of the bicycle patrol supervisor may be taken to a private bicycle repair shop, utilizing procurement procedures established by the College. Maintenance and/or repairs that are covered under warranty and/or a service agreement should be taken to the designated repair shop. All receipts for repairs/maintenance performed must be submitted for procurement processing.
Make recommendations for equipment to be placed out of service.
Maintain a service log. Bicycle patrol officers, other than the supervisor, who make repairs on the patrol bicycles, shall make the appropriate entries in the service log.
The following equipment shall be carried on each police bicycle:
Lock - handcuffs may be used instead
Spare tube and tire changing tools
Bicycle patrol officers shall be familiar with the operation of all equipment used by the unit.
Officers shall only utilize those bicycles authorized by the Department. Officers shall not operate, remove or alter any bicycles or equipment without the approval of the bicycle patrol supervisor.
During periods when bicycles and equipment are not in use, they shall be placed in the designated secured storage location.
